summary: Design a realistic end-to-end BrotherSBE collaboration flow for a two-timezone product team, group by group, then refute every claim against the tool as it actually is

checked.group: PRODUCT (PM for development, two Business Analysts, Designer, Integration Manager)

roles.role: PM for development
roles.owns: Accountable for what enters the sprint and for the state of every change in flight; the only person who sees both the Tokyo commercial side and the offshore build queue. BrotherSBE changes none of that accountability and assigns no work.
roles.artifact_they_produce: 08-plan.json (derived from the approved dossier by `sbe plan`) and one `sbe work brief --plan 08-plan.json --task <id> --json` per task handed offshore
roles.artifact_they_consume: `sbe status --team`, a blocker-first view over changes that have RECORDED state under design/, findings ranked on a 1..11 severity ladder with a `basis` field, plus the tier in each 00-intake.json
roles.what_changes_for_them: One thing, and it is the handoff. Instead of a Slack paragraph, the night dev receives a byte-identical JSON work order carrying scope, mustNotTouch, dependencies, acceptance, verificationCommands, knownConstraints and stopConditions, so the 2am ambiguity has a written answer. What does NOT change: nothing prevents a ticket entering the sprint without an intake file, because BrotherSBE has no connection to a tracker and cannot block anything. 'Every ticket carries a 00-intake.json' is a rule the PM enforces by hand, the same way any other team convention is enforced. `sbe status --team` shows changes somebody recorded and is blind to the rest, so it is a view of the process, not of the work, and it does not replace the standup.

roles.role: Business Analyst (lead on a change)
roles.owns: Turns a commercial request into a tiered dossier and defines what 'correct' means before code exists. This is a writing job that the tool checks the shape of, not the substance of.
roles.artifact_they_produce: design/<change>/00-intake.json always; then only what the tier owes: T0 nothing, T1 one artifact, T2 six, T3 seven (01-purpose.md, 02-process.md, 07-verification.md and the rest)
roles.artifact_they_consume: the commercial request, the Integration Manager's 05-data-model.md, and at merge time the `sbe converge --base <kickoff sha> --head <PR head>` verdict if somebody runs it
roles.what_changes_for_them: On a request like contract pricing for liquor retailers with vouchers applied on top, the BA answers five fixed questions (`sbe intake design/retailer-contract-pricing`) and a decision table returns the tier. The rule is fixed, the ANSWERS are not: the BA supplies them, and a BA who answers 'no' to the money question gets T0 and owes nothing. Nothing at intake time contradicts a wrong answer. `sbe impact` reconciles the declared tier against what a diff touched, but that is later, after code exists, and it reasons from changed paths, not from what the change means. Second honest point: of the artifacts the BA writes, only ADR shape, data-model shape, diagram node tracing, artifact presence and the shipped-template placeholder are machine-checked. Nothing reads 01-purpose.md, 02-process.md or 07-verification.md for content. A purpose brief of one thin sentence passes every check that ships. The real gain is a habit, that the reconciliation check for discounted line totals gets written before the pricing code, and the habit is what has to be defended, not the gate.

roles.role: Business Analyst (second seat, as refuter)
roles.owns: Reviews the other BA's dossier against the diff. This seat is a human review and BrotherSBE does not replace it, shorten it, or vouch for it.
roles.artifact_they_produce: a review verdict on the dossier and, where a change touches money or partner data, the `Approved-by:` commit trailer on a signed commit
roles.artifact_they_consume: `sbe design --strict design/<change>` (artifacts, adr, datamodel, diagrams, placeholder) and `sbe impact`
roles.what_changes_for_them: Three of the five checks do real mechanical work for them: the placeholder check names any file still carrying the shipped template, the adr check refuses an ADR without two distinct rejected alternatives and a flip condition, the datamodel check refuses an entity with no system of record or a relationship with no cardinality. Everything else is still their judgment, including whether the system of record named is the right one, which no check can reach. On the approval gate, read the fine print before relying on it: it PASSes on Approved-by only when the host verified the signature against a key it trusts (git %G? = G and nothing weaker), so a Jenkins agent with no imported reviewer keys produces %G? = E and the gate does not pass. The fallback Reviewed-in path proves only that a non-vacuous id string is present. Self-approval fails, which is what makes the two-BA structure worth having. And nothing anywhere detects that a change NEEDED an approval; the gate only verifies one that was declared.

roles.role: Designer
roles.owns: Screen states and interaction across the mobile app, shop web app and portal web app.
roles.artifact_they_produce: frames for the exception states, and whatever they choose to write into the exception-path column of 02-process.md
roles.artifact_they_consume: 02-process.md, when a T2 or T3 change produces one
roles.what_changes_for_them: Almost nothing, and less than a first reading suggests. BrotherSBE has no opinion on visual design, accessibility, content quality or copy, and no check reads a Figma file. It also does not check that a process step named an exception path: the template asks for one, the design checks only verify the file is present and is not still the shipped example. So the exception-path discipline is a convention the BA and Designer keep, with no enforcement behind it. It only applies at T2 and T3 at all, so most work never touches it. The residual value is a meeting habit, that stale, empty, partial-sync and vendor-unreachable states get named in Tokyo hours rather than invented offshore at 2am, and on a Pimcore and Strapi stack syncing through RabbitMQ into Elasticsearch those states are the common ones. If the team wants more for the Designer than a habit, this is not the tool.

roles.role: Integration Manager
roles.owns: Every seam to Pimcore, Strapi, LINE Connect, Voucherify, Klaviyo, Branch.io, Firebase and Cognito. Each is a contract nobody wrote down.
roles.artifact_they_produce: 05-data-model.md (entities with a named system of record, relationships with cardinality, plus the source and failover table), 03-adr.md per seam decision, 04-technology-map.md, and the .sbe/policy.yml rules binding integration paths to required evidence
roles.artifact_they_consume: the BA's 02-process.md, and `sbe policy evaluate` verdicts on a diff when somebody runs it
roles.what_changes_for_them: This role gains the most, and the gain is narrow enough to state exactly. Identity is the example that bites this stack: a LINE user, a Cognito sub and a Customer row are three identifiers for one person, and the mapping lives in one head and in whatever CustomerSync does. In 05-data-model.md that becomes three named entities each with a declared system of record and a cardinality on every relationship, and the datamodel check FAILs if any of those is missing. It checks that the field was FILLED, never that the answer is right: writing Pimcore where the truth is the Product service passes. The Voucherify redemption-ownership question gets an ADR with two rejected alternatives and a flip condition, so reopening it next year is a lookup instead of an excavation. The source and failover table (refresh contract, behaviour when unavailable, per source) is the piece to insist on, and it is unchecked prose, so its quality is entirely on this person. 04-technology-map.md rows are unchecked too. Nothing introspects any vendor.

today_without_sbe: A commercial request arrives as a thread and a Figma frame, becomes a ticket description, and is implemented eight timezones away by someone who hits an unanswered question at 2am. Blocking costs a day, guessing costs nothing visible, so guessing wins and surfaces in QC or in a POS cron job disagreeing with the Order service a week later.

Nobody has written which system is the system of record for a given field. Product master in Pimcore, content in Strapi, price in the Product service, cached in Redis, indexed in Elasticsearch, read by three client apps. When the shop web app shows a wrong pack size, the first hour of the incident is spent deciding which of five stores was supposed to be right.

Eight external integrations have no written contract and the Integration Manager holds all of them. When a vendor changes a payload field, a queue processor's broad catch swallows it, Sentry shows nothing because nothing threw, and a customer finds the failure.

Cardinality is decided in code. Product variant to SKU to retailer-specific price list is many-to-many on this business and gets implemented as one-to-many by whoever writes the sync first. It is discovered when a retailer sees a price from someone else's contract.

Nothing at merge time re-reads the request the change was approved from three weeks earlier. The two-reviewer-plus-Tech-Lead rule on Bitbucket reviews the diff, so the thing that ships is judged only against itself.

There is no objective rule for how much design a change owes, so the team runs two modes, 'it's just a ticket' and 'it's a project'. In practice the money path is under-taxed, because the pressure is always toward shipping.

The two BAs are the only people who can answer intent questions and they are asleep for the whole offshore build window. Every ambiguity is either an eight hour stall or an undocumented decision made by someone with no view of the commercial contract behind it.

with_sbe.step: BA runs intake on the commercial request. Five fixed questions, one tier out, written into the change's directory. For a T0 change this is the ONLY step, and the process ends here.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: mkdir -p design/retailer-contract-pricing && python3 tools/sbe_intake.py design/retailer-contract-pricing  (writes 00-intake.json with the five answers and the computed tier; an answer outside the declared vocabulary is refused by name rather than guessed at)
with_sbe.who_does_it: Business Analyst (lead)
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: The negotiation over how much design a change owes, and equally the over-taxing of small work: T0 owes nothing and is the common case, T1 owes one artifact. It does NOT prevent a wrong answer. The tier is computed from what the BA typed, and nothing at this moment checks that against reality.

with_sbe.step: For T2 and T3 only, the BA writes purpose and process. Every step names an actor, a trigger and an exception path, and every handoff names a contract.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: design/retailer-contract-pricing/01-purpose.md and 02-process.md (templates in templates/dossier/)
with_sbe.who_does_it: Business Analyst (lead), with the Designer on the exception states
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: The 2am guess, by convention rather than by gate. 'Voucherify unreachable' and 'no contract price for this retailer' get named while Tokyo is awake. Be clear that no check reads these files for content: the design checks verify the file exists and is not the shipped template, nothing more.

with_sbe.step: For T2 and T3, the Integration Manager writes the data model: system of record per entity, cardinality and optionality per relationship, plus the source and failover table naming each source, its refresh contract and its behaviour when unavailable.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: design/retailer-contract-pricing/05-data-model.md, checked by the datamodel design check
with_sbe.who_does_it: Integration Manager, reviewed by the second BA
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: The five-stores-and-nobody-knows-which-is-right incident, to the extent that writing it down prevents it. The check enforces that a system of record is NAMED and a cardinality is STATED. It cannot tell a correct answer from a confident wrong one, and the failover table is unchecked prose.

with_sbe.step: One ADR per seam decision, each with named criteria, two distinct rejected alternatives, the decision, consequences and a flip condition.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact:
03-adr.md; optionally printf '5
eventual
high
high
' | python3 tools/sbe_decide.py tables/architecture.json shape for the architecture shape call, where a run in which no criterion contributed returns NO-DATA and suppresses the recommendation
with_sbe.who_does_it: Integration Manager with the PM
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Archaeology when Voucherify changes redemption semantics next year. The adr check enforces the SHAPE (two distinct rejected alternatives, a flip condition present). It does not judge whether the alternatives were real or the flip condition meaningful, and the decision itself stays a human decision.

with_sbe.step: Write the verification artifact before the build: every claim, the check that proves it, when it runs.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: 07-verification.md
with_sbe.who_does_it: Business Analyst (lead)
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: QC inventing acceptance criteria three weeks later, and the discounted-line-total reconciliation being written by the person who wrote the pricing code. Unchecked for content, so this is discipline, not enforcement.

with_sbe.step: Run the five design checks strict on the dossier before the work is handed offshore. A human decides what to do with the result.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: python3 tools/sbe_design.py --strict design/retailer-contract-pricing  (artifacts present, adr, data model, diagrams tracing to declared entities, placeholder)
with_sbe.who_does_it: Business Analyst (second seat) or PM
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A dossier that exists but says nothing, in the three places a check can reach. The placeholder check naming files still carrying the shipped example is the single highest-value line here, because that is how a design gate turns into theatre. It stops nothing by itself: exit codes only matter once somebody wires them into a Jenkins stage.

with_sbe.step: PM derives the plan from the approved dossier, then mints one work order per task for the night shift.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: sbe plan (writes 08-plan.json), then sbe work brief --plan 08-plan.json --task T01 --json (sorted keys, no timestamp, byte-identical across runs; scope, mustNotTouch, dependencies, acceptance, verificationCommands, knownConstraints, stopConditions; refused rather than truncated past 8192 bytes)
with_sbe.who_does_it: PM for development
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: The handoff paragraph. stopConditions is the field that pays for itself across a timezone boundary: it names what to stop on rather than work around, turning an eight hour stall into a written escalation. It does not decide who does the work and does not schedule anything.

with_sbe.step: Transfer ownership across the boundary explicitly. Ownership does not move until a named human on the receiving side acknowledges.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: sbe handover prepare | show | acknowledge | reject (writes 12-handover.json)
with_sbe.who_does_it: PM on the Japan side, offshore lead acknowledging by running the command themselves
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: The silent handoff where work is assumed picked up. Reject is a first-class outcome and leaves the outgoing owner as owner. It notifies nobody, wakes nobody and enforces no response time; the receiving human has to run acknowledge for the record to exist at all.

with_sbe.step: Integration Manager writes policy rules for the seam paths so a change touching them is asked for evidence.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: .sbe/policy.yml with path globs and content signals, evaluated by sbe policy evaluate on a diff; verdicts SATISFIED, MISSING, INVALID, STALE, UNPROTECTED, NOT-REQUIRED, with MISSING exiting nonzero
with_sbe.who_does_it: Integration Manager
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: The bypass where a change avoids declaring anything and so avoids the gate, and the confusion between 'entitled to carry nothing' (NOT-REQUIRED) and 'the evidence is absent' (MISSING). Two limits: it evaluates a diff when somebody runs it, so it requires nothing before code is written, and a path nobody thought to glob is a path nobody is asked about. It blocks a merge only if a Jenkins stage the team wrote calls it.

with_sbe.step: At merge time, compare the diff against the dossier it was approved from rather than against itself.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: sbe converge --base <commit the design was implemented from> --head <PR head> design/retailer-contract-pricing  (scope, contracts, data, architecture, verification; no force flag exists), plus sbe impact
with_sbe.who_does_it: Business Analyst (second seat)
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Three weeks of drift landing unexamined. It is a mechanical comparison along five declared dimensions, not a judgment about commercial intent, and it can only be as good as the dossier it compares against. It cannot block the merge; a human reads the verdict and decides, inside the existing two-reviewer-plus-Tech-Lead review, which it does not replace.

integration_points.system: Bitbucket (branch permissions and merge checks)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: The dossier is committed as design/<change>/ in the same repository as the code, so it is reviewed in the same pull request under the existing rules.
integration_points.mechanism: The team writes a Bitbucket merge check pointing at a Jenkins job, plus branch permissions on main. BrotherSBE ships no branch protection, no merge checks and no CI configuration. What it does ship is a GitHub Actions workflow in its own repository (.github/workflows/brothersbe-gates.yml), which is a reference to be re-expressed as Jenkins stages, not something this team can use.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Bitbucket pull-request approval evidence (sbe pr verify, sbe protections verify)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Nowhere on this team.
integration_points.mechanism: Those two surfaces read the GitHub API through gh and read a CODEOWNERS file plus a GitHub branch ruleset. This team is on Bitbucket and has no CODEOWNERS. Both commands are dead here. The only host-independent approval path is the signed Approved-by commit trailer below.
integration_points.confidence: not possible

integration_points.system: Jenkins
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Stages the team writes on the existing PR-open, push-to-PR-branch and merge-to-master triggers: design completeness, the four hard gates, the silent-failure linter, and a converge stage before auto-deploy to Staging.
integration_points.mechanism: python3 tools/sbe_design.py --strict design/<change>, python3 tools/sbe_gate.py --strict design, python3 tools/sbe_score.py --strict --strict-soft ., sbe converge --base <merge-base> --head $GIT_COMMIT. Every one of these stages has to be authored, tuned and maintained by this team. Outside --strict the tools print a verdict and exit 0, so until the stages exist nothing blocks and nothing changes in CI.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Commit signing for the approval gate
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: The approval gate PASSes on Approved-by only when git reports %G? = G, a signature verified against a key the host trusts, and the trailer names somebody other than the author and committer.
integration_points.mechanism: Reviewers sign commits and the Jenkins agents import the reviewers' public keys into a trust store somebody maintains. Without that, agents report %G? = E and the gate does not pass, leaving only the Reviewed-in id path, which proves a non-vacuous string is present and nothing else. Key distribution and rotation are the team's to build.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Pimcore (PIM, product master data)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Named as system of record for product master entities in 05-data-model.md, with refresh contract and behaviour-when-unavailable in the source table.
integration_points.mechanism: A committed markdown file, read by the datamodel design check for presence of a system of record on every entity and a cardinality on every relationship. This is not an integration with Pimcore. Nothing introspects Pimcore class definitions, and a well-formed wrong answer passes.
integration_points.confidence: ships today

integration_points.system: Strapi (CMS)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: The CMS-owned versus PIM-owned field split, declared per entity, so the ProductSync mapping has one written owner instead of two plausible ones.
integration_points.mechanism: Same committed 05-data-model.md and the same presence check. The 02-process.md handoff row naming the Strapi-to-sync-to-Product-service contract is unchecked prose; only the entity-level declarations are read by anything.
integration_points.confidence: ships today

integration_points.system: Voucherify, Klaviyo, Branch.io, LINE Connect, Firebase, Cognito
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: One ADR per seam decision, plus handoff rows in 02-process.md and component rows in 04-technology-map.md.
integration_points.mechanism: Only the ADR shape is checked (two distinct rejected alternatives, a flip condition, no shipped template text). The 02 and 04 rows are unchecked prose held to standard by the Integration Manager alone. There is no validation against any vendor's live schema and no test that a declared contract matches what a vendor sends. The claim is that the seam becomes reviewable by a human, and nothing beyond that.
integration_points.confidence: ships today

integration_points.system: RabbitMQ queue processors (Notification, CartSync, OrderSync, ProductSync, CustomerSync)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Each processor appears as an actor in 02-process.md and each queue as a handoff with a stated contract.
integration_points.mechanism: That process artifact is unchecked prose, so nothing verifies a queue's ack window or its not-consumed behaviour was written at all. The silent-failure linter that would catch the swallow patterns making a dead processor look healthy covers .py .sql .swift .rb .js .ts .go and does NOT read C#, so it is silent on these .NET processors, and it only runs in CI once the team writes the stage.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: SQL Server (primary) and the data warehouse
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: The migration gate reads migration-receipt.json (forward and reverse both run against a restored copy, a rehearsal id, matching row counts). The numbers gate reads numbers-manifest.json (a pinned snapshot, a second derivation textually different from the first, re-run to zero drift).
integration_points.mechanism: BrotherSBE reads receipts. It does not produce them. Somebody on this team has to build the migration rehearsal job against a restored copy and the reconciliation job that emits the manifest, then wire python3 tools/sbe_gate.py --strict as a stage. A receipt with no row counts is NO-DATA, and NO-DATA is never a pass. Nothing resolves the rehearsal id against Jenkins or any job system.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: SonarQube and Gitleaks in the existing CI
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Partial overlap only. The silent-failure linter looks for bare except, except-then-pass, discarded subprocess result, conflict-skipping upsert and force-try.
integration_points.mechanism: python3 tools/sbe_score.py --strict --strict-soft . as an extra stage the team adds. It reads SQL in any host language, which is the one place it commonly adds something over default Sonar rules on warehouse work. It does not read C#, so the Identity, Product, Customer, Order, User and Cart services are outside it, which is most of the estate.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Sentry (release tag and commit pushed by CD)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Only by shared commit sha. sbe lineage <artifact> walks binding, receipts, decisions, notes and commits with an evidence pointer per hop.
integration_points.mechanism: Nothing in BrotherSBE reads Sentry and no automatic link exists between a Sentry release and a dossier. The join from a production error back to the design is done by a human or by a script this team writes.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket issues
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Nowhere.
integration_points.mechanism: No tracker integration of any kind exists. The dossier is files in the repository, and the link from a commercial request to design/<change>/ is a line a BA types by hand. If they stop typing it, the chain breaks silently and nothing reports that.
integration_points.confidence: not possible

integration_points.system: HashiCorp Vault
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Nowhere. BrotherSBE holds no secrets and injects none.
integration_points.mechanism: No integration exists and none is planned. Secrets stay in the existing Vault-to-Helm path.
integration_points.confidence: not possible

integration_points.system: EKS, Helm, the manual production approval with its one hour timeout
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: It drafts the command and its rollback. It never runs either.
integration_points.mechanism: No apply rights on production, ever. It cannot deploy, cannot approve, cannot merge. The one hour approval window belongs to a human and BrotherSBE cannot see, consume or extend it.
integration_points.confidence: not possible

integration_points.system: The vault of notes (BROTHERSBE_VAULT)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Telemetry, session logs and resume briefs, so a change's history survives a session ending in Tokyo and resuming offshore.
integration_points.mechanism: export BROTHERSBE_VAULT=<path>, on every machine and every CI agent that should write to it. Unset, bin/sbe doctor reports NO-DATA on it by name rather than folding it into the passes. The install does not set it, and nothing syncs it between the two sites.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

release_points: Before work is handed offshore: 00-intake.json exists and its tier says how many artifacts are owed. This is the earliest point and the only one that is purely Product's. It is enforced by the PM and the BAs as a convention, not by any tool, because BrotherSBE is not connected to the tracker or the sprint.

Pull request opened on Bitbucket: sbe design --strict on the dossier, but only once the team has written the Jenkins stage and pointed a Bitbucket merge check at it. Nothing about opening a PR triggers BrotherSBE out of the box.

Push to the PR branch: sbe impact reconciles the declared tier against what the diff touched, and sbe policy evaluate reports MISSING (nonzero) for a required check with no receipt. Same condition: a stage the team wrote, calling these with the right base and head.

Merge to master: the four hard gates strict plus the silent-failure linter, again as team-authored stages. Absent evidence is NO-DATA and NO-DATA is never a pass, so a change with nothing to prove is not taxed and a change that should have proved something is not let through on an empty directory. The linter is silent on the .NET services at this point and every other.

Auto-deploy to Staging: sbe converge over the range against the approved dossier. Advisory output unless the team makes the stage blocking. No force flag exists, but a red verdict a human ignores is still a merged change.

Pre-Production, for SQL Server schema work: the migration receipt (forward and reverse against a restored copy, rehearsal id, matching row counts) and, on money and partner-data paths, the signed Approved-by trailer verified against a trusted key. Both depend on jobs and key management this team builds first. Nothing detects that a change should have carried either.

Manual production approval with the one hour timeout: BrotherSBE has drafted the command and its rollback and collected receipts. A human runs it. Nothing in the tool approves, deploys or merges, and it cannot see the one hour clock.
honest_limits_for_this_group: BrotherSBE blocks nothing on its own. Every gate in this section is a command that prints a verdict and, with --strict, exits nonzero. Turning an exit code into a stopped merge is Jenkins stages plus Bitbucket branch permissions and merge checks that this team writes and maintains. Until those exist, adopting BrotherSBE changes what people write, not what CI does.

Two of the surfaces that verify approval are GitHub-only and unusable here: sbe pr verify reads the GitHub API through gh, and sbe protections verify reads CODEOWNERS and a GitHub branch ruleset. This team has neither. The only portable approval evidence is a signed commit trailer, which needs reviewer public keys imported on the Jenkins agents before it can ever pass.

Nothing detects that a change NEEDED an approval. The gate verifies an approval that was declared. .sbe/policy.yml narrows this for paths somebody thought to glob, and a path nobody globbed is a path nobody is asked about.

The tier is computed from five answers a human types. The rule is fixed and unarguable; the inputs are not checked against anything. A BA who answers 'no' to the money question gets T0 and owes nothing, and no check at intake time disagrees. sbe impact can raise a tier later from what a diff touched, which is after the code exists and reasons only from paths.

Only ADR shape, data-model shape, diagram-to-entity tracing, artifact presence and the shipped-template placeholder are machine-checked. Nothing reads 01-purpose.md, 02-process.md, 04-technology-map.md or 07-verification.md for content. A thin dossier written to clear the gate clears the gate, and sbe converge then compares the diff against that thin thing.

The data model check verifies a system of record is NAMED and a cardinality is STATED, never that either is correct. Writing Pimcore where the truth is the Product service passes every check that ships.

The Designer gains close to nothing. No check reads a Figma file, the tool has no opinion on visual design, accessibility, content quality or copy, and no check verifies that any process step declared an exception path. What is left is a habit of enumerating failure states in Tokyo hours, worth something on a sync-heavy stack, and it only applies at T2 and T3.

The silent-failure linter covers .py .sql .swift .rb .js .ts .go and does not cover C#. The core services and every queue processor are .NET, so it fires on the front ends, the SQL and Python tooling and is silent on the largest part of this estate.

The numbers gate proves two derivations differ in TEXT, not that they are independent. Two queries over the same broken Elasticsearch projection or the same wrong warehouse view both pass. Renaming an alias passes. Nothing reads which tables either derivation touches.

Nothing resolves the migration rehearsal id against Jenkins or any job system. It is a string in a receipt and a pointer for a human to follow. BrotherSBE also does not produce the receipt; the team builds the rehearsal and reconciliation jobs that emit it.

sbe handover records that a named human acknowledged ownership. It wakes nobody, notifies nobody, enforces no response time, and reject leaves the work with the outgoing owner. It makes the state honest; it does not make the timezone smaller.

Nothing here replaces a human review, a standup, or a decision. The two-reviewer-plus-Tech-Lead rule stays exactly as it is, sbe status --team reads only recorded state and is blind to work nobody recorded, and it does not manage people or assign anything.
There is no tracker integration at all. The link from a commercial request to design/<change>/ is a line a BA types, and if they stop typing it the chain breaks with no signal.

This is a real cost on two BAs. A T3 change owes seven hand-written artifacts, and the whole defence is that T0 owes nothing and is meant to be the common case. Nobody has measured this team's T0/T1/T2/T3 mix. Measure it on four weeks of real requests before committing the group, because if the mix skews to T2 and T3 the two BAs become the bottleneck for the entire pipeline.

Every threshold BrotherSBE ships was measured on ONE estate, not this one, and not on a two-timezone team with a night shift. Treat the tier boundaries and the check selection as a starting position to argue with after a month, not as calibrated defaults.

checked.group: DEVELOPMENT: the Full Stack lead, two Front End developers, the Night Dev BE and the Night Dev FE (offshore, working the Japan night across a daily timezone handover)
honest_limits_for_this_group: THE LINTER DOES NOT READ C#, AND PROBABLY DOES NOT READ THE FRONT END EITHER. The extension list is exactly (".py", ".sql", ".swift", ".rb", ".js", ".ts", ".go") at tools/sbe_score.py:655. There is no .cs, so every .NET microservice, every RabbitMQ queue processor and every cron job is invisible. There is also no .tsx, no .jsx and no .vue. If the shop and portal web apps are React or Vue, which is the common case and which nobody has confirmed to me, then the two Front End developers and the Night Dev FE get the linter over almost none of their real files either. Verify the actual extensions in those repositories before promising this group anything from the linter. No configuration adds an extension today.

NO-DATA DOES NOT BLOCK A MERGE. `--strict` exits nonzero only on FAIL (tools/sbe_gate.py: `if verdict == "FAIL": fails += 1`, then `if strict and fails: sys.exit(1)`). A NO-DATA verdict prints, and the build exits 0. So "NO-DATA is never a pass" is true about the verdict and false about the exit code. A change that declares no evidence at all sails through every gate.

NOTHING DETECTS THAT A CHANGE NEEDED A RECEIPT. The migration gate returns NO-DATA with the literal reason "no migration in this change, or no migration-receipt.json": it cannot tell those two apart. Same for approval and numbers. A night developer who writes an Order schema migration and mints no receipt gets a clean-looking run. The gates verify declared evidence; they never notice absent evidence.

THE WRITE FENCE ONLY BINDS CLAUDE CODE SESSIONS, AND IT FAILS OPEN. tools/sbe_fence_hook.py is a Claude Code PreToolUse hook on Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit (hooks/hooks.json), and its own rule 1 is FAIL OPEN, LOUDLY: every failure path allows the write. A developer typing in Rider, Visual Studio, VS Code or any IDE is not fenced at all, and neither is `git apply` or a shell redirect outside the guarded tools. For a team of humans this is not an enforcement boundary.

`sbe work start` DOES NOT COMPARE FILE SCOPES BETWEEN WRITERS. It refuses when the branch exists, when the worktree directory exists, or when that task id already has an OPEN registry record. Two people can open two different tasks whose scopes overlap completely and both starts succeed. Scope comparison lives only in the Claude Code hook above. So the collision story for the Japan front end developers and the Night Dev FE is a visible registry a human has to read, not a refusal.

CONVERGE AND THE REVIEWER ROUTER CANNOT CLASSIFY C# EITHER. converge's source extension set is (".py", ".sql", ".md", ".sh", ".js", ".ts", ".go", ".rb", ".java", ".kt", ".json", ".yaml", ".yml", ".toml", ".cfg", ".ini", ".txt"). A grep for .cs, .tsx and .jsx across impact.py, converge.py, reviewroute.py and sbe_score.py returns nothing. A changed .NET file that no impact detector recognizes lands in an explicitly unmeasured category, not in a verdict.

CI-CLAIMED IS NOT PROOF THAT JENKINS RAN IT. src/brothersbe/evidence.py says in its own words that CI-CLAIMED means CI shaped metadata was recorded, and that the seal is not a signature: anybody who can read the file can compute a matching one. Any developer who exports SBE_CI_RUN_ID on a clean tree gets CI-CLAIMED on a laptop receipt. Trust here rests on Jenkins being the only place that variable is set, which is a convention the team enforces, not something the tool proves.

`sbe pr verify` SPEAKS THE GITHUB API AND ONLY THE GITHUB API (src/brothersbe/prverify.py: API_ROOT = "https://api.github.com"). On Bitbucket it cannot run at all. The only approval path that works here is the signed git commit trailer, and it PASSes only when the CI host verified the signature against a key it already trusts. Until the signers' public keys are on the Jenkins agent, every approval reads NO-DATA, and per the point above NO-DATA does not stop anything.

NO CI CONFIGURATION SHIPS FOR JENKINS AND NO MERGE CHECK SHIPS FOR BITBUCKET. The reference is a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/brothersbe-gates.yml). There is no CODEOWNERS, no branch protection, no ruleset, and nothing in this plugin can create any of those. Until somebody writes the Jenkins stage and the Bitbucket merge check, every command in this document is advisory text next to a merge button that still works.

REVIEW-ROUTE PREVENTS NOTHING. It prints at most two suggested specialist roles from the diff. It does not add reviewers to a Bitbucket pull request, does not enforce the two-reviewer rule, does not know who is awake, and its own module says mechanicalOnly or a null primary reviewer never means the change is clean. It is a suggestion a human may ignore, and the Bitbucket branch permission remains the only thing that actually requires two humans.

THE HANDOVER RECORD IS A FILE, NOT A LOCK. `handover acknowledge` refuses on a stale record and refuses a self-handover, which is real. But nothing stops the lead from merging, deploying or ignoring the record entirely. Ownership does not move in any system; it moves in a JSON file that both people have agreed to read.

openQuestions, decisions and requiredAccess ARE WRITTEN EMPTY. The engine derives done, inFlight, notStarted, active tasks, worktree dirtiness and evidence freshness. The one thing a 06:00 JST handover most needs, the open question, is typed by a human or it is not there.

NOTHING READS A .NET DTO, AN OCELOT ROUTE FILE, A RABBITMQ BINDING, A MESSAGE SHAPE, A DEAD LETTER POLICY OR A HELM CHART. A contract change to Order or Product is caught only to the extent that a person wrote the contract into 02-process.md and 05-data-model.md by hand. There is no consumer impact analysis of a C# type, and no deploy-ordering check for a publisher and its consumer.

THE NUMBERS GATE PROVES TWO DERIVATIONS DIFFER IN TEXT, NOT THAT THEY ARE INDEPENDENT. Two queries over the same broken Order view both pass. The `ran` gate proves a check exited zero and took nonzero time; it does not know whether the integration test tests what its name says. That judgement stays with the QC engineers.

IT CANNOT DEPLOY, MERGE OR APPROVE, AND NEVER GETS APPLY RIGHTS ON PRODUCTION. It drafts the command and its rollback for a human to run. The one hour manual production window in Jenkins is exactly as human as it was before, and nothing here participates in the Osaka failover.

THE COMMON CASE IS T0, WHICH OWES NOTHING. tools/sbe_intake.py: REQUIRED["T0"] is the empty list. A CSS fix, a copy change, a log line: the honest output of this whole method is one 00-intake.json and no dossier. Any process that makes a front end developer write an ADR for a T0 change has misused the tool, and that is the most likely way this dies inside a team of four developers.

THE TWO FRONT END DEVELOPERS GAIN THE LEAST, AND POSSIBLY NOTHING AUTOMATED. The tool has no opinion on visual design, accessibility, component quality or copy. If their files are .tsx, the linter reads none of them, and the write fence does not bind their IDE. What is left for them is the deterministic work brief and a registry they can read, which is a coordination convention rather than a control. Their real benefit is indirect: the night shift hands back a record instead of a sentence.

THE SPINE OF THE METHOD, DESIGN BEFORE VERIFICATION AND INSTALL THE CHECK BEFORE WRITING THE WORK, IS A STATED DISCIPLINE. No tool computes it. A team that stops writing dossiers gets a set of gates reading files nobody maintains, and every verdict above degrades to NO-DATA, which does not block.

EVERY THRESHOLD HERE WAS MEASURED ON ONE ESTATE. The handover, evidence, impact and converge surfaces are marked INTERNAL-EVAL in this repository's own documentation: they ran against this project's fixtures and its own diff, against nobody else's, and never against a .NET microservice estate.

Bitbucket pull request open, and every push to the PR branch: nothing runs until the team writes the Jenkins stage. Once written, the design checks, the four gates and the linter produce verdicts a night developer can read without waiting for a Japan morning. Note what the linter reads: .ts, .js and .sql, not .cs and not .tsx.

Merge to master: the same commands with --strict, wired to a Bitbucket merge check the team creates. Only a FAIL exits nonzero. A change that declares no migration receipt, no approval trailer and no numbers manifest produces three NO-DATA lines and exits 0, so this stops bad declared evidence, never absent evidence.
Auto-deploy to Staging: `sbe converge` over base..head, if the team adds it as a stage. It has no force flag, and its blind spot on this estate is large, since it cannot classify a .cs file.

Pre-Production: the migration gate, but only if a Jenkins job restored a copy, ran forward and reverse, and wrote the receipt. This is where a broken rollback should surface, hours before the production window, and it will surface only for changes where somebody minted the receipt.

Manual production approval in Jenkins, one hour timeout: the approver can read 12-handover.json and the gate verdicts instead of a pull request description. BrotherSBE never touches the button and the one hour clock is unchanged.
Osaka DR failover: entirely out of scope. Nothing participates in a semi-automated failover or a DNS redirect.

He still reads the C# himself, still writes the ADR, still picks the architecture, still presses the production approve button. What he actually gains is a written record of what the night shift finished, left half done and never started, at a specific commit.

roles.what_changes_for_them: Honestly, very little, and possibly nothing automated. The write fence only intercepts Claude Code's edit tools and fails open on any error, so their IDE is unfenced. `sbe work start` does not compare file scopes between two tasks, so it will not refuse a collision either; the registry is something a human reads. The linter covers .ts and .js but has no .tsx or .jsx, so if these apps are React it reads almost none of their files, and somebody must check that before this is promised to them. The tool has no opinion on their components, layout, accessibility or copy. Most of their work computes T0 and correctly owes nothing at all. Their real gain is indirect: the night shift hands back a record instead of a sentence.

roles.role: Night Dev BE (offshore, .NET microservices, the RabbitMQ queue processors, the cron jobs)
roles.owns: Responsible for back end implementation during the Japan night, with no synchronous access to the person who designed the change.
roles.artifact_they_produce: Receipts from `sbe evidence run --check <id> --kind gate`, migration-receipt.json when the change touches a SQL Server schema and somebody remembered to mint one, and 12-handover.json prepared at end of shift naming the Full Stack lead as receiver

The shift opens on a byte-identical JSON work order and a dossier committed in the repository, instead of reconstructing intent from a channel written while they were asleep. A stop condition becomes a recorded stop and an open question rather than eight hours of guessing. Everything downstream of that is weaker than it looks: the linter never opens their C#, converge cannot classify their .cs files, and if they mint no migration receipt the gate reports NO-DATA and the build still exits 0. Nothing tells anyone they should have minted one.

roles.role: Night Dev FE (offshore, same shop and portal repositories the Japan front end developers own by day)
roles.owns: Responsible for front end implementation during the Japan night against repositories two other people write to during the Japan day.
roles.artifact_they_produce: A registry record and worktree on their own branch, receipts for the commands they ran, and their half of 12-handover.json
roles.artifact_they_consume: The work brief for their task, the fence list, and the outgoing handover record from the Japan day side
roles.what_changes_for_them: The collision with the Japan day side becomes visible earlier, but it is not prevented. `sbe work start` refuses a taken branch, a taken worktree path or a re-opened task id, and does not compare their file scope against anyone else's. The only thing that compares scopes is a Claude Code hook that binds nobody typing in an IDE. So this is a declared-scope convention that surfaces overlap to a human who reads the registry, not a refusal at claim time. The linter's coverage depends on whether these apps are .ts or .tsx, which nobody has confirmed. The tool says nothing about the interface they built.

today_without_sbe: A contract change to Order service goes up as a Bitbucket pull request at 02:00 JST. The Business Analyst who knows why the field exists is asleep. The PR sits until 10:00 JST, review lands at 11:00, the night developer is asleep by then, and one round trip on a DTO rename costs a full 24 hours.

The reason behind a decision lives in a channel scrollback. Why ProductSync is eventually consistent, why Pimcore and not Product service is the system of record for price, why the Ocelot rate limit sits where it does: all decided in Japan hours, none of it written into the repository, so a night developer either guesses or blocks.

A DTO on Product service changes shape while the ProductSync processor and the Pimcore push still consume the old one. Nothing in the pull request states which consumers exist, so the mismatch surfaces as Sentry noise in Staging the next Japan morning rather than as a review comment.

A RabbitMQ processor change ships with no stated deploy ordering. Consumer goes out before publisher, or the reverse, and in-flight messages in the old shape sit in the queue with no drain plan recorded anywhere.

A migration against the Order schema is "tested locally" and the reverse was never run against a restored copy. The rollback turns out to be broken at the production approval window, which has a one hour timeout, with the author asleep on the other side of the timezone.

The manual production approval in Jenkins is granted on the strength of a pull request description. The approver in Japan and the author on the night shift never overlap, so the approval attests to a summary rather than to anything that ran.

Two Japan front end developers and one night front end developer touch the same cart components inside one 24 hour cycle with no declared file scope anywhere, so the overlap is discovered as a merge conflict.

SonarQube decorates the pull request and says nothing about whether the change owed any design at all. A catch-and-continue inside a queue processor either passes the default ruleset or gets waived with no recorded reason, and a swallowed exception in an async consumer is exactly the failure class that looks identical to success.

The handover itself is a sentence in a chat window at 06:00 JST. Nobody can query it later, "I told them" cannot be checked, and there is no record of what was finished, what was half done, what was never started, or what question was left open.

REQUIRED["T0"] is the empty list, so a copy change or a CSS fix produces one small JSON file and no dossier. An Order change touching money or production state lands T3 and owes seven artifacts; a Product catalogue contract change with many consumers lands T2 and owes six.

It cannot tell whether the decision recorded is a good one, or whether it matches the C# anybody later writes.

What it does not prevent: a laptop receipt looking like a CI one. The seal is not a signature, and CI-CLAIMED only means SBE_CI_RUN_ID was set on a clean tree, which anyone can do.

with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe gate design/<change>. Where a migration receipt exists it must record forward AND reverse both run against a restored copy, matching row counts, and a rehearsal id. A receipt with no row counts is NO-DATA, not a pass.

with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Discovering at the one hour production approval window that a down migration recorded in a receipt was never actually executed. It prevents nothing at all when no receipt was written: the gate emits NO-DATA with the literal reason "no migration in this change, or no migration-receipt.json", and --strict exits nonzero only on FAIL, so that run still passes. Reading a clean gate report as "this change is safe" is the exact misreading to guard against.

with_sbe.step: The handover is a file bound to a commit instead of a sentence at 06:00 JST
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe handover prepare design/<change> --outgoing "<night dev>" --receiver "<full stack lead>", writing 12-handover.json. Everything except the two identities and three fields is derived: done, inFlight and notStarted from 08-plan.json against .sbe/tasks.json; active tasks with agent, role, worktree and base commit; every worktree and the repository root checked for uncommitted state; every evidence item tagged current, stale or unavailable; one deterministic nextAction sentence. openQuestions, decisions and requiredAccess are written EMPTY and must be typed by the human.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Night Dev BE or FE, at end of shift
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A lead starting the day by reading scrollback, and uncommitted work sitting in a night worktree nobody knows exists. It does not capture the open question, which is the thing a 06:00 handover most needs, unless a person writes it.

with_sbe.step: The receiving lead accepts or rejects in writing, at the same commit
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe handover show design/<change>, then acknowledge --receiver "<name>" or reject --receiver "<name>" --reason "CartSync consumer not updated". Acknowledge refuses outright on a stale record, naming both shas. A receiver that reads as the outgoing owner is refused at both ends.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Full Stack lead, Japan morning
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Accepting code that moved after the handover was prepared, self-handover, and a rejection that leaves no trace of why. It does not gate anything downstream: this is a record two people agree to keep, and nothing stops a merge or a deploy that ignores it.

with_sbe.step: Before Staging, the diff is compared back to the dossier, with its blind spot stated
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe converge over base..head across scope, contracts, data, architecture and verification. No force flag, and none may be added.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Full Stack lead, or a Jenkins stage the team writes
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A branch quietly growing a path, an entity or a declared component nobody designed, between the approved dossier and the merge, for the file types it understands. Its source extension set contains no .cs, no .tsx and no .jsx, so on a .NET plus modern front end estate a large share of the diff falls into a category it explicitly reports as unmeasured rather than as a verdict.

with_sbe.step: A deterministic reviewer suggestion, which is a suggestion
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe review-route: at most two specialist roles derived from the changed files, no model chooses, zero specialists is a legal result and never means the review was clean
with_sbe.who_does_it: Whoever opens the pull request
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A migration or a security surface going unnoticed because nobody thought to mention it. It does not add reviewers to the Bitbucket pull request, does not enforce the minimum-two rule, and does not know who is awake. The Bitbucket branch permission stays the only thing that requires two humans, and a human review is not replaced by any of this.

with_sbe.step: The silent-failure linter runs over the file types it can actually read
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe score --strict --strict-soft . across exactly .py .sql .swift .rb .js .ts .go. A reviewed exemption carries a visible `# sbe: allow-silent <reason>` marker in the diff; a bare marker or one saying `tbd` waives nothing. A run that opened no file is NO-DATA naming why, never "clean".
with_sbe.who_does_it: Every developer locally, and a Jenkins stage once written
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A conflict-skipping upsert in raw SQL, or a swallowed error in a plain .ts file, reading as success. Confirm the actual file extensions in the shop and portal repositories before promising the front end anything: there is no .tsx and no .jsx in the list. There is no .cs either, so every .NET service, queue processor and cron job is outside it entirely.

checked.group: QC (three QC engineers, offshore, against a .NET microservice estate on Bitbucket and Jenkins, where AI writes a growing share of the code)

roles.role: QC engineer, staging automation lane (E2E, performance, security suites)
roles.owns: Responsible for the automated suites that run against Staging after auto-deploy, and accountable to the Tech Lead for whether a build is fit to promote. BrotherSBE changes none of that ownership: it runs no tests and makes no promotion decision.
roles.artifact_they_produce: Today: a green Jenkins stage plus a console log. With BrotherSBE, only after the team writes the Jenkins stage: a sealed ran-receipt per suite carrying the check id, the argv resolved from .sbe/checks.yml, the exit code, a nonzero duration, headCommit, and content digests of the paths the registry entry DECLARES the check covers (not everything the suite actually touched). Its trust level tops out at CI-CLAIMED, never at a level that proves it came from CI.
roles.artifact_they_consume: 07-verification.md from the dossier, when the change has one at all (T0 owes none, and T0 is the common case), plus whichever reviewer reports the deterministic router named for that diff.
roles.what_changes_for_them: They stop pasting a Jenkins job name into a PR comment and start pointing at a receipt path in the branch. `sbe evidence verify <receipt>` fails by name if headCommit moved or a declared covered path changed bytes. New work lands on them at the same time: every suite they want counted as evidence needs a registry entry they write and maintain, and editing that entry invalidates receipts minted before the edit. The receipt does not tell them the suite asserted anything.

roles.role: QC engineer, pre-production UAT lane (product owner sign-off)
roles.owns: Responsible for running the UAT pass in Pre-Production and getting the product owner's sign-off recorded. The sign-off stays a human decision that BrotherSBE neither makes, prompts for, nor notices the absence of.
roles.artifact_they_produce: Today: a ticket comment naming a person and a date. With BrotherSBE, only if the signing prerequisites are built: an Approved-by trailer on a commit, signed with a key the host running the gate already trusts (git %G? = G and nothing weaker), naming somebody other than the author and committer. The gate's strongest sentence requires the named approver's own key to be the one that signed; a trailer naming the PO on a commit signed by a developer is a weaker verdict, not the same thing.
roles.artifact_they_consume: Acceptance criteria in 07-verification.md where a dossier exists, the qa-reviewer's traceability prose, and the evidence-auditor's prose verdicts on the receipts in front of them. Both reviewer outputs are model-written prose, not computed checks.
roles.what_changes_for_them: Honestly, this is the thinnest role of the three in the near term, because the mechanism is only as good as a key the product owner does not have today. If a commercial-side product owner never touches git and holds no signing key, the gate returns NO-DATA (git %G? = E on a runner with no imported keys, or U for a self-generated key), and NO-DATA is never a pass. The keyless Reviewed-in: path is also NO-DATA, because nothing resolves the id. So on a Tuesday this lane's realistic gain is smaller: receipts bound to the commit the PO exercised, so a rebase visibly breaks the binding, while the sign-off itself stays a human record until somebody builds the key trust.

roles.role: QC engineer, dev lane and night-shift handover coverage
roles.owns: Responsible for the shift boundary: reviewing what the Night Dev BE and Night Dev FE pushed while Japan slept and deciding whether it is testable before the Japan-side day starts. That decision stays theirs.
roles.artifact_they_produce: A verdict on whether the branch is testable. With BrotherSBE, if a QC engineer opens a Claude Code session on the diff: the qa-reviewer report on a test-only diff, and the evidence-auditor's freshness reading of any receipt inherited from the previous shift. Neither runs in Jenkins; both are a person invoking an agent.
roles.artifact_they_consume: The diff, at most two routed specialist reports (zero when nothing triggers), and receipts whose staleness is a command rather than a timestamp read out of a rotating console log.
roles.what_changes_for_them: The 09:00 question becomes `sbe evidence verify` for the narrow question of what ran, against what commit, for how long. The bound: the stale-receipt refusal fires only when the receipt actually records a headCommit. A receipt naming no commit is not refused, and the gate cannot tell a missing field from an operator who chose not to record one. Nothing here says why a test failed, and nothing here reads the .NET services the night shift most often changes.

roles.role: Check-registry and evidence owner (rotating across the three)
roles.owns: New responsibility BrotherSBE creates rather than removes: owning .sbe/checks.yml entries for QC-owned suites, and owning the honest reading of NO-DATA.
roles.artifact_they_produce: Registry entries binding a check id to an executable, an argument vector, a working directory and covered paths, plus a running record of which QC obligations are registered and which are listed unregistered with a reason.
roles.artifact_they_consume: The policy engine's list of what a change is required to carry, and the gate verdicts PASS, FAIL or NO-DATA, where NO-DATA is never a pass.
roles.what_changes_for_them: They gain a file that is protected control plane, meaning a change to it owes control-plane evidence and an approval. Stated flatly: that is a policy the engine reports on, not a lock. Nothing prevents the edit landing unless Bitbucket branch permissions and a required Jenkins stage make it so, and neither ships. The honest gain is narrower than 'the command stops being a string in a Jenkinsfile': the receipt records the spec digest and runner hashes so a changed check invalidates prior receipts, but the Jenkinsfile still decides whether the check is invoked at all, and BrotherSBE cannot see a stage somebody deleted.

today_without_sbe: A green Jenkins stage is a property of a job run, not of a commit. It does not say the suite ran after the last push to the PR branch, which tests were skipped rather than passed, or whether the assertion count changed. Zero tests executed with exit code 0 renders green in every reporter they have.

The three-level review (Technical, Security, Business) is recorded as human approvals on a Bitbucket pull request. Nothing in that record distinguishes a Business reviewer who mapped acceptance criteria to tests from one who approved because the status-check column was green.

AI-written code raises the volume of plausible code with plausible tests. A test written from the fix, by the same generator that wrote the fix, confirms the author's own assumption. Nothing in the pipeline asks whether re-injecting the defect makes that test fail.
SonarQube, Gitleaks and Trivy are artifact scanners. None of them says whether an acceptance criterion has a test, which is the question QC is asked at Pre-Production.

The timezone split separates the code that gets reviewed from the code that gets tested by a handover. By the time Japan-side QC looks, the only artifact tying a pass to a state of the tree is a Jenkins console log that rotates.
Pre-Production UAT sign-off is a comment naming a person and a date, not bound to a commit. A hotfix rebased onto pre-prod leaves the sign-off reading as valid over code the PO never exercised.

Reconciliation numbers on the sync surfaces (ProductSync, CustomerSync, OrderSync, CartSync, Pimcore and Strapi syncs, the Invoice, POS and Report crons) get quoted into reports. When a second derivation is run, nobody records that it was, so a quoted total and a verified total look identical on the page.
Migration evidence is a developer's word. Whether the reverse migration ran against a restored copy, and whether row counts matched, lives in memory or a chat message.

with_sbe.step: Skip the design phase entirely on T0 changes, and read the verification phase only where the intake actually produced one.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: 07-verification.md, which exists only at T1 and above. T3 owes seven artifacts, T2 six, T1 one, T0 nothing.
with_sbe.who_does_it: The QC engineer on the lane that will own the suite, alongside the Business Analyst who wrote the criteria.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: On the minority of changes that carry a dossier, it prevents an acceptance criterion with no executable test surfacing at UAT. Stated as a bound rather than a benefit: T0 is the common case, so for most changes there is nothing to read and adding a dossier step there is ceremony the tier explicitly does not owe. Nothing computes whether the verification phase was written before the branch or backfilled after the merge.

with_sbe.step: Register each QC-owned suite as a check id so evidence identity is declared rather than inferred from a command line.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: .sbe/checks.yml entry per suite (executable, exact argv, working directory, covered paths, runner files).
with_sbe.who_does_it: The rotating registry owner among the three QC engineers, with Tech Lead approval on the control-plane change.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: The documented defect where a receipt for `/bin/cat tests/test_design_of_gate_score.txt` named three obligations in its argv and cleared all three. `--check <id>` refuses substitution of the executable, argv, coverage or kind on the command line, and `--kind` must be declared. It does not prevent a registry entry pointing an important-sounding id at a script that exits zero.

with_sbe.step: Have the team write a Jenkins stage that wraps the existing Staging suites in the evidence runner.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: `sbe evidence run --check e2e-staging` and its performance and security equivalents, inside a Jenkins stage the team authors. BrotherSBE ships no Jenkinsfile, no pipeline library and no CI configuration.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Staging automation lane QC engineer plus whoever owns the Jenkinsfile.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A hand-typed receipt. Duration and exit code come from the subprocess or the receipt does not exist, and the seal is tamper evidence against hand authoring. Correcting a common overstatement: setting SBE_CI_RUN_ID does not prove the run happened in CI. The best trust level any receipt reaches is CI-CLAIMED, whose own text says a run id was recorded and nothing verified who set it. A laptop that exports SBE_CI_RUN_ID on a clean tree gets the same level.

with_sbe.step: Add a gate stage, and run it in strict mode, knowing the gate still cannot block anything by itself.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: `sbe gate ran --strict` as a Jenkins stage. Without `--strict` the gate is advisory and exits 0 no matter the verdict. Making the stage required to merge is Bitbucket branch permissions and merge checks, configured by the team.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Staging automation lane QC engineer plus the Jenkinsfile owner; the merge check is whoever administers the Bitbucket repository.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Three greens that are not passes: a receipt recording zero checks (NO-DATA, never a pass, enforced at check construction), a receipt with zero duration, and a receipt whose recorded headCommit is not current HEAD. The third fires only when headCommit is present; a receipt recording no commit is treated exactly as it always was.

with_sbe.step: Let the deterministic router pick reviewers from the diff, and read only what it routes.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: Seven read-only specialists, at most two named per change, zero when nothing triggers, T0 and T1 capped at one. The route is computed from the diff, not chosen by a model; the reports themselves are model-written prose.
with_sbe.who_does_it: A QC engineer running a Claude Code session on the change. This is a person opening a tool, not a pipeline step.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A fourth review level. The reviewers cannot approve, merge or write code, so they replace no human reviewer and no standup. What they save is traceability bookkeeping, and only when a trigger fires.

with_sbe.step: Point qa-reviewer at test-only diffs to catch the specific way generated fixes turn green.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: qa-reviewer, routed on rule 6 over a test-only diff: an assertion removed with none added back, a skip or xfail marker added with no replacement assertion, or a significant test-only line count with no weakening signal.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Runs read-only under whichever QC engineer holds the change. It cannot edit a test.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: The deleted or skipped failing assertion. Its output is prose a human reads and judges, including the calibration question of whether re-injecting the defect makes the test fail. No number comes out and no threshold fires, and the line-count threshold that decides whether it looks at all was measured on one estate that is not this one.

with_sbe.step: Attack the receipts before Pre-Production with a role structurally barred from producing them.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: evidence-auditor, read-only, verdicts CONFIRMED, UNVERIFIED or REFUTED per piece of evidence, with an explicit list of what it did not attack.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Pre-Production UAT lane QC engineer runs it. The auditor never generates the evidence it audits.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Evidence trusted because it is well formatted: a zero-duration run, a row count matching a stale figure, a rehearsal id that resolves to nothing, a CI-CLAIMED receipt read as if somebody had verified its origin. Its verdicts are argued prose, not computed facts, so they persuade a human rather than block a pipeline.

with_sbe.step: Bind receipts to the commit the product owner exercised, and treat the signed trailer as a later goal rather than a Monday change.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: Receipts carrying the same headCommit as the change. The Approved-by trailer becomes mechanical only once the approver holds a signing key and the host running the gate trusts its public half.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Pre-Production UAT lane QC engineer collects it; the product owner signs, if and when signing exists for them.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A sign-off surviving a rebase. Two limits, both large: nothing detects that a change needed an approval, so somebody must still declare that a release owes a PO sign-off; and until keys are imported, the gate answers NO-DATA rather than approving, which is correct but is not the artifact the team wanted.

with_sbe.step: Re-verify at the Pre-Production to Production boundary rather than trusting the earlier run.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: `sbe evidence verify <receipt>`, which recomputes headCommit against current HEAD, the digests of the declared covered paths, the check spec digest, the runner file hashes and the seal.
with_sbe.who_does_it: The QC engineer on the release, before the manual production approval opens its one hour window.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Promoting on evidence that describes a different program. It does not gate the promotion. BrotherSBE never gets apply rights on production, cannot deploy and cannot approve; the manual approval and its timeout stay entirely with the human who holds them, and nothing in BrotherSBE observes whether that human ran the verify at all.

integration_points.system: Jenkins (CI: build, tests, Gitleaks, SonarQube, Docker, Trivy, ECR)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: The test stage and one new gate stage, both of which the team writes. BrotherSBE replaces no scanner and configures nothing.
integration_points.mechanism: Stages the team authors: `sbe evidence run --check <id>` per QC suite, then `sbe gate ran --strict` whose nonzero exit fails the build. Default mode is advisory and exits 0, so a stage without `--strict` reports and blocks nothing. Nothing in BrotherSBE reads the Jenkinsfile, so a stage that is removed, renamed or made non-blocking is invisible to it.

integration_points.system: Bitbucket (repository host, PRs)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: The dossier, receipts and reviewer reports are ordinary committed files, so they arrive in the PR as a diff and as paths a reviewer can open. No host API is involved.
integration_points.mechanism: A committed dossier directory plus receipt JSON in the branch, linked from the PR description by a human. Safe to attach because stdout and stderr are stored as SHA256 digests and byte counts only.
integration_points.confidence: ships today

integration_points.system: Bitbucket branch permissions and merge checks (making a gate actually block a merge)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Nowhere. It cannot make a check required, and it cannot merge, approve or deploy.
integration_points.mechanism: Bitbucket branch permissions and merge checks configured by the team, requiring the Jenkins gate stage to pass. No CODEOWNERS, no branch protection, no CI configuration and no GitHub ruleset ships, and GitHub Actions is not in this picture at all.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Bitbucket API verification of those merge checks
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: `sbe pr verify` and `sbe protections verify` exist and shell out to `gh api`. There is no Bitbucket client.
integration_points.mechanism: None. On this estate both commands make zero useful requests and return NO-DATA per network fact they cannot check, and NO-DATA is never a pass. Whether the merge check is actually required is a question a person answers by looking at Bitbucket on a schedule they set.
integration_points.confidence: not possible

integration_points.system: .sbe/checks.yml (the check registry inside the protected control plane)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Where QC's E2E, performance and security suites become declared check ids instead of inferred command lines.
integration_points.mechanism: One entry per suite, written and maintained by QC, naming executable, argv, working directory, covered paths and runner files. `verify` recomputes the spec digest and runner hashes, so a renamed runner or changed argument invalidates prior receipts. Protected control plane means the policy engine says a change to it owes evidence and an approval; it is not a lock, and nothing stops the edit landing without Bitbucket permissions behind it.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: The .NET core services (Identity, Product, Customer, Order, User, Cart, and the queue processors)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: The silent-failure linter does not read them. Its scannable set is .py, .sql, .swift, .rb, .js, .ts, .go. There is no .cs.
integration_points.mechanism: None as shipped. Front-end .ts and .js, .sql, and any Python tooling are covered. C# swallowed exceptions and discarded results stay a SonarQube and human-review problem. Extending the extension set is a change to BrotherSBE itself, not a setting the team can flip.
integration_points.confidence: not possible

integration_points.system: SQL Server and the data warehouse (migrations, reconciliation queries, BI numbers)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: The migration gate and the numbers gate, which read files the team produces.
integration_points.mechanism: The gates ship; the evidence does not. Somebody has to build a restored-copy rehearsal that runs forward and reverse, records a non-blank rehearsal id and records row counts on both sides (a migration receipt with no row counts is NO-DATA, not a pass), and somebody has to write a genuinely second derivation against a pinned snapshot id. Until that process exists, the gates report NO-DATA.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Git signing trust (the prerequisite for the approval gate meaning anything)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: The approval gate reads git's own verification result on the host where the gate runs.
integration_points.mechanism: The approver needs a signing key, and its public half must be in the allowed signers or keyring trusted by that host. Without it, git reports %G? = E and the verdict is NO-DATA; a self-generated SSH key reports U, also NO-DATA. The gate's strongest sentence needs the named approver's own key to be the signer, so a developer rebasing a commit that carries somebody else's Approved-by is a weaker verdict, not an approval.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Sentry (release tag and commit pushed at deploy)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Only by shared commit sha. No Sentry client, no knowledge of releases.
integration_points.mechanism: The receipt's headCommit is the same sha Jenkins pushes to Sentry, so a release can be joined to its receipt set by a script or a human the team writes. Nothing in BrotherSBE performs that join.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: HashiCorp Vault (secrets injected at deploy)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Indirectly, through what a committed receipt records.
integration_points.mechanism: stdout and stderr are stored as SHA256 digests and byte counts only, so a suite that prints a connection string does not persist it into the shared artifact. The caveat that keeps this honest: the argv, working directory and covered paths ARE recorded verbatim, so a credential passed as a command-line argument is committed in the clear. Keep secrets in the environment, never in a registry entry.
integration_points.confidence: ships today

integration_points.system: Pimcore (PIM) and Strapi (CMS) and their sync jobs
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Only where a sync writes SQL Server or produces a reconciliation number.
integration_points.mechanism: Pimcore class definitions and Strapi content-type changes are not schema migrations it recognises, and it has no opinion on content quality. A content change that breaks a downstream contract may be visible to a reviewer reading the diff; no gate covers it.
integration_points.confidence: not possible

integration_points.system: The seven read-only specialist reviewers against the existing three-level review
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Before the human review, never inside it. Exactly one role can write code and it reviews nothing.
integration_points.mechanism: A QC engineer opens a Claude Code session on the change and reads at most two routed reports. That presumes offshore QC engineers have Claude Code access and repository checkout, which is an access and licensing question the team has to settle before any of this is real. None of the reviewers can approve or merge, so none is a fourth level and none replaces the Technical, Security or Business reviewer.
