release_points: Development (Osaka, isolated EKS): receipts minted here are LOCAL-ADVISORY, and a dirty tree keeps them there. Useful for the reviewers and the linter, not as release evidence.

Pull request opened against feature/xxx on Bitbucket: the reviewer route is computable here and the linter can run here, but only if somebody runs them. Design checks are answerable here for the minority of changes above T0.

Push to the PR branch: the point that matters most for QC, because it is where a previously green run goes stale. The ran gate refuses a receipt whose recorded headCommit is not current HEAD, and does nothing about a receipt that recorded no commit.

Merge to master (minimum two reviewers, Tech Lead approval, status checks, linear history, no force push): the approval gate reads a signed Approved-by trailer if one exists and if the host trusts the key. Bitbucket enforces the merge. BrotherSBE cannot merge, cannot approve, and cannot tell that an approval was owed.
Staging (Tokyo EKS, auto-deploy): the QC suites, once wrapped by a stage the team writes, mint receipts bound to a commit and to declared covered paths. Trust level CI-CLAIMED at best.

Pre-Production (Tokyo EKS): UAT with product owner sign-off. evidence-auditor can be run before the sign-off; its output is prose for a human. The sign-off stays a human record until signing keys exist.

Production (manual approval with a one hour timeout, rolling update): `sbe evidence verify` is worth re-running here, by a person. BrotherSBE never gets apply rights, drafts commands and rollbacks for a human to run, and neither sees nor influences the approval or its timeout.
Hotfix/xxx: the same gates apply, and the stale-receipt refusal is the point of them. A rebase orphans receipts that recorded a commit, and breaks the signature on any signed approval trailer.
DR failover to Osaka (active-passive, semi-automated, under four hours): nothing here. No receipt, no gate, no reviewer covers a failover rehearsal.
honest_limits_for_this_group: There is no achievable trust level that proves a run came from CI. The code's own text: a run id recorded on a clean tree yields CI-CLAIMED, and nothing verified who set it. SBE_CI_RUN_ID is an ordinary environment variable, so a laptop can produce the same level, and the seal is a checksum over the receipt's own fields, not a signature. Any claim that a laptop run can never be read as a CI run is false.

The .NET services are not covered by the silent-failure linter. Its scannable set is .py, .sql, .swift, .rb, .js, .ts, .go, with no .cs. For a team whose Identity, Product, Customer, Order, User and Cart services are all C#, this is the single largest gap for this group, and no configuration closes it.

`sbe pr verify` and `sbe protections verify` go through `gh api` and have no Bitbucket client. On this estate they report NO-DATA. Whether a gate is actually required to merge is audited by a person in Bitbucket, on a cadence QC sets.

The gates are advisory by default and exit 0. Only `--strict` fails a build, only a Jenkins stage the team writes runs it, and only a Bitbucket merge check makes that stage matter. Three separate pieces of the team's own wiring sit between a FAIL and a blocked merge.

Nothing reads the Jenkinsfile. A stage deleted, renamed, or quietly moved off the blocking path is invisible to every check here, so 'which command counts as the E2E check' is protected only for receipts that were actually minted.

The ran gate proves a registered check exited zero in nonzero time against the current commit. It does not prove the check asserts anything. A registry entry pointing an important-sounding id at a script that exits zero passes.

The stale-receipt refusal depends on an optional field. A receipt that records no headCommit is not refused, and the gate cannot distinguish a missing field from an operator who chose not to record one.

Nothing detects that a change needed an approval. The gate verifies an approval that was declared. If nobody declares that a release owes a product owner sign-off, its absence is silent, which is exactly the Pre-Production UAT case.

The approval path is not usable on day one. A signature the host cannot verify is NO-DATA (%G? = E, the normal result on a runner with no imported keys), a self-generated SSH key is NO-DATA (U), the keyless Reviewed-in: path is NO-DATA because nothing resolves the id, and a bare typed name FAILs. A product owner who does not use git cannot produce the artifact at all until somebody builds key trust for them.

The numbers gate proves two derivations differ in TEXT. It does not prove they are independent. Two queries over the same broken view, or two reads of the same stale Elasticsearch index, both pass. For sync reconciliation across Pimcore, Strapi and SQL Server this matters, because the easy second derivation is the same derivation rephrased.
Nothing resolves a rehearsal id against a job system. It is a pointer for a human, and a migration receipt naming a rehearsal that never ran is syntactically clean.

BrotherSBE runs no tests. It drives no browser, no load generator and no scanner. The E2E, performance and security suites, their fixtures, environments and flakiness remain entirely QC's. It changes only what the result of running them is worth as evidence.
There is no flake computation. qa-reviewer writes prose about retries, sleeps, order dependence and shared state. No number, no threshold.

The reviewers and the evidence auditor produce model-written prose that persuades a human. They compute nothing, block nothing, and replace no reviewer, no standup and no decision. Reading them is time added to three offshore engineers' day, and it presumes they have tool access and a checkout, which nobody has confirmed.

The spine of the method, design before verification and install the check before writing the work, is a stated discipline. No tool computes it. A 07-verification.md written after the merge passes everything downstream.
T0 is the common case and owes nothing, so the design-phase benefit applies to a minority of changes. Adding dossier ceremony to T0 work is cost with no gate behind it.

Every threshold shipped, including the test-only line count that decides whether qa-reviewer looks at a coverage change, was measured on one estate that is not this one. The project states plainly that it has never run in anyone else's CI and claims no second estate. Expect retuning and a period where the router fires too often or not enough.
It has no opinion on visual design, accessibility, content quality or copy. For a team with seven Content Specialists running a PIM and a CMS, that is a large surface of QC work it does not reach.

It cannot deploy, cannot approve, cannot merge, and never gets apply rights on production. It produces the artifact a human gate reads. If that gate is a rubber stamp today, it will be a rubber stamp over better artifacts tomorrow.

today_without_sbe: A Pimcore class field change is made in the admin UI in the Japan afternoon. It never enters a Bitbucket diff, so no PR opens, no Jenkins job runs, SonarQube decorates nothing, and no reviewer is selected. The first place it becomes visible is a ProductSync consumer failing in Sentry or a null appearing in Elasticsearch, seen hours later by the Night Dev BE with nobody awake to ask what changed.

Nobody has written down which store is the system of record. Pimcore holds product master data, Product Service holds its own SQL Server tables, Elasticsearch holds a derived index, and Strapi holds copy that also carries product-shaped fields. When the shop web app shows a wrong pack size, the first hours go to arguing which store is right instead of fixing it.

Bulk content edits have no reconciliation. Thousands of SKUs go into a mass attribute update; nobody counts what came out of ProductSync into SQL Server, and nobody counts what landed in the Elasticsearch index. A silent drop of a few hundred records is indistinguishable from success.

A field deletion, retype or enum narrowing has no rehearsed reverse. The previous class definition exists only inside Pimcore's own storage, and no one has restored a copy and put it back to find out whether that works.

Strapi content-type changes ship on the CMS cadence and Product Service changes ship on the Jenkins cadence, so the portal web app can receive a content-type field the Product Service build has never heard of, and the ordering of the two releases is decided in chat.

The CD pipeline's manual production approval with its one hour timeout governs code deploys only. A Pimcore publish and a Strapi publish reach production without passing Development, Staging or Pre-Production at all, because they are classified as data, not as a release.

with_sbe.step: Make the shapes visible to git at all. Export Pimcore class definitions and mirror Strapi content-types into a Bitbucket path that a shipped detector matches, for example schemas/pimcore/<Class>.json and schemas/strapi/<type>.json. This is a build job the team writes; BrotherSBE ships nothing that does it. Without this step every item below is inert, because every check reads a git diff, a JSON file or a markdown file and none of them can see the Pimcore admin UI.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: A Pimcore definition export committed on a branch (confirm the export command and on-disk path against the installed Pimcore version, do not assume). The path matters: the shipped event-schema detector is r"(^|/)(events?|schemas?)/.*\.(json|ya?ml|avsc)$" in src/brothersbe/impact.py, which needs a DIRECTORY named event, events, schema or schemas.
with_sbe.who_does_it: PIM schema owner, with a Development engineer to write and own the export job
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Nothing on its own. It is the precondition that makes a field shape change reviewable at all, instead of invisible until the night shift sees Sentry.

with_sbe.step: Tier the change with the five-question intake instead of assuming all content work is equal. Adding an optional marketing attribute consumed only by Strapi answers no to every question and computes T0, which owes nothing and runs no dossier ceremony. Renaming a price-bearing field on the product class answers yes to money, which computes T3 and owes all seven artifacts.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe intake design/pim-price-field (the tool takes the dossier directory as a positional argument and asks the five questions on stdin; it writes 00-intake.json into that directory)
with_sbe.who_does_it: PIM schema owner
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Both failure directions: ceremony on the routine attribute edit, which is the common case here, and a silent uncontrolled change to a field Order and Cart price against. Note the intake is self-declared: nothing stops a person answering no five times.

with_sbe.step: Reconcile the declared tier against the actual diff. impact converts detector hits into the same five answers a human gives and hands them to the same compute_tier, so a declared T0 over an exported class definition under schemas/ is raised to T2 (the event-schema detector sets changes_contract, and changes_contract computes T2). It may raise a tier and may never lower one; consumers is assumed at its lowest value and reported under unmeasured, and every changed file no detector covers is listed by name.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe impact . --base origin/main --intake design/pim-price-field/00-intake.json --strict
with_sbe.who_does_it: The schema owner locally, and a Jenkins stage the team writes and maintains. BrotherSBE ships no Jenkins job.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A shape change declared as routine content work, but only for files a detector covers and only after the definitions are in the repository. It does not reach T3 by itself on most price work: the money detector matches path words like pricing, discount and invoice, not the bare word price, so a file named PriceList.json raises to T2 and no further.

with_sbe.step: Write down the system of record, once, for real. The data-model design check fails until every entity names its system of record and every relationship carries a cardinality: Pimcore is SoR for product master data, SQL Server is a replica written by ProductSync, Elasticsearch is a derived index, Strapi is SoR for editorial copy only. The diagram check then fails if a node appears that traces to no declared entity.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: design/<change>/05-data-model.md and 06-diagrams.md, checked by bin/sbe verify
with_sbe.who_does_it: PIM schema owner with a Business Analyst
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: The two-hour argument about which store is right during a live catalogue incident. This is a human writing down a decision; the check only enforces that the fields are filled, not that the answers are true. It is still the single highest-value thing this group can produce and it does not exist today.

with_sbe.step: Rehearse the reverse before the forward runs, then record it. The migration gate reads a hand-written migration-receipt.json carrying a forward leg, a reverse leg, matching row counts and a rehearsal id. For a Pimcore field change the reverse is re-importing the previous definition export, which only exists because of the export step above.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: A rehearsal the team performs in the Development environment (Osaka, isolated EKS), transcribed into design/<change>/migration-receipt.json; a receipt with no row counts is NO-DATA, not a pass
with_sbe.who_does_it: PIM schema owner plus a Development engineer; the restore, the rehearsal and the transcription are all theirs
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A field delete or retype with no way back, discovered at the moment somebody needs the way back. The gate proves a person wrote down that both legs ran. Nothing resolves the rehearsal id against any job system, and nothing observed the restore.

with_sbe.step: Write down the counts on a bulk change, from both sides of the sync. The numbers gate wants a second derivation whose text differs from the first beyond case, whitespace, comments and trailing punctuation, a pinned snapshot_id, and two numbers that match exactly.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: design/<change>/numbers-manifest.json, checked by bin/sbe gate numbers <dir> --strict. Optionally register the count command in .sbe/checks.yml and wrap it with bin/sbe evidence run --out <path> --kind gate --check <id>, which produces a ran-receipt for the ran gate; the executable and its arguments come from the registry and nothing on the command line replaces them.
with_sbe.who_does_it: The Content Specialist authoring the bulk change
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A silent partial sync going unnoticed, only if a human chose to count on opposite sides of the boundary. The gate proves two queries differ in wording, not that they are independent, and the figures are transcribed, not measured.

with_sbe.step: Get a second named human on a money-bearing shape change. This is a discipline the team imposes; BrotherSBE only examines an approval that was already declared. On the signed path the Approved-by identity is compared against the commit author and committer, with bidi controls and mixed-script words refused by name, so self-approval fails.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: A commit signature the verifying host can check plus an Approved-by: trailer. Reviewed-in: <Bitbucket PR id> returns NO-DATA, never PASS, so it is a pointer for a human, not an approval.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Business Analyst or Integration Manager as approver; a Development engineer must import signer public keys into the Jenkins agent's keyring or the strong path never returns PASS on this estate

release_points: Pimcore publish and Strapi publish, the real release point for this group today: content reaches production without traversing Development, Staging or Pre-Production. BrotherSBE does not gate this and cannot. At most it makes the SHAPE half of the change appear in a Bitbucket PR that does traverse the ladder, and only after the team builds the export.

Development (Osaka, isolated EKS): the only environment where a forward-and-reverse rehearsal against a restored Pimcore plus SQL Server copy is honest. The rehearsal is the team's work; BrotherSBE reads the written claim that it happened.

Staging (Tokyo, auto-deployed by Jenkins on merge): where the content-contracts PR lands and where a re-synced product shape first meets a running Product Service, ProductSync consumer and Elasticsearch index together.

Pre-Production (Tokyo, same EKS, dedicated node groups): where the two count derivations should be run at a data volume close to production, because a reconciliation on a thin Staging dataset proves nothing about a bulk change over the real catalogue. The counts are run by people and transcribed into the manifest.

Production: the Jenkins manual approval with a one hour timeout governs the code deploy only, and it is Jenkins that enforces it, not BrotherSBE. A content shape change riding the content-contracts repo inherits that gate; a Pimcore or Strapi publish does not.

The daily Japan-to-offshore boundary, which functions as a release point whether or not anyone calls it one: bin/sbe handover writes the transfer down and withholds the word transferred until the named receiver acknowledges. It sends nothing and blocks nothing.
honest_limits_for_this_group: The direct benefit to this group is thin and should be presented that way. Most of what seven Content Specialists do all week is values, copy, imagery and categorisation. Those changes compute T0, and T0 owes zero artifacts, runs no gates and produces no dossier. The tool touches perhaps a handful of changes a quarter: the ones that alter the SHAPE of product data. Five or six of the seven feel nothing directly.

It cannot see the Pimcore admin UI, and this is the load-bearing limit. Every check, gate and detector reads a git diff, a JSON file or a markdown file. A field edited and saved in Pimcore and never exported to a repository is invisible to all of them, and nothing notices the omission. Without the export-and-commit job, which the team builds and BrotherSBE does not ship, everything above is inert for this group.

The numbers gate does not run anything. Verified in tools/sbe_gate.py: it reads numbers-manifest.json and checks that the two derivation texts differ beyond case, whitespace, comments and trailing punctuation, that a snapshot_id is pinned, and that two transcribed numbers are equal in value and unit. The numbers are typed by a person. It has no database connectivity, cannot re-execute a query, and cannot tell a transcribed figure from an invented one. It also proves nothing about independence: two counts taken downstream of the same broken ProductSync agree and are both wrong.

On Bitbucket there is no passing approval path without signed commits. Verified in tools/sbe_gate.py: Reviewed-in: <PR id> returns NO-DATA, never PASS, because the gate does not resolve the id against any review platform. The only PASS is a signature this host verified against a key it trusts, carrying an Approved-by trailer, which means a Development engineer must maintain a keyring on the Jenkins agent. Without that, the approval gate is permanently NO-DATA for this group, and under --strict that blocks rather than approves.

Nothing detects that a change NEEDED an approval. The approval gate only examines an approval somebody already declared. If the intake is answered as T0, no approval is ever demanded. impact can raise a tier from the diff, but only for files a detector covers and only after the definitions are in the repository.

The money detector matches path words like payment, billing, invoice, pricing, discount and rebate. A file named PriceList.json or ProductPrice.json does not match, so a price-bearing Pimcore class exported under schemas/ raises to T2 on the contract detector and no further. Reaching T3 on price work depends on a human answering the money question honestly.
The rehearsal id is a string. Nothing resolves it against any job system. Restored a copy and re-imported the previous definition is a claim a human makes and another human must check.

BrotherSBE ships no CODEOWNERS, no branch protection and no CI configuration. Bitbucket branch permissions, merge checks and the Jenkins stages are the team's to write and maintain. Nothing in the plugin blocks a merge, and pr verify reads GitHub only (API_ROOT is https://api.github.com), so it is unusable on this estate.

It never gets apply rights. It cannot publish or unpublish a Pimcore object, trigger a re-sync, reindex Elasticsearch, deploy, approve or merge. It drafts the command and its rollback for a human to run.

It has no opinion on content quality or copy. It will not tell you a description is wrong, a translation is poor, an image is missing, a category tree is illogical, a price is a typo, or that a product is unpublished when it should be live. A fully gated change can ship completely wrong content and every gate will pass.

It does not manage people, assign content work, or replace the content standup, and it replaces no human review. The Business Analyst review it references has to be requested by a person and performed by a person; the gate at most checks that two identities differ.

The spine (design before verification, install the check before writing the work) is a stated discipline that no tool computes. If the group writes the dossier after the field change already shipped, every gate can still pass.

The cost is real and lands on one nominated person. A four-minute Pimcore rename becomes an export, a branch, an intake, a dossier and a wait for a second human. If the group will not staff a PIM schema owner, none of this happens and the honest answer is that BrotherSBE does nothing for CONTENT.

Every threshold shipped was measured on one estate, and impact is marked INTERNAL-EVAL: run on the plugin's own repository fixtures and its own diff. Nothing here has been run against a Pimcore or Strapi installation, and the detector-path claims above were verified by reading src/brothersbe/impact.py, not by exporting a real Pimcore class.

roles.artifact_they_produce: Jenkins stages that call bin/sbe, the branching logic that decides which SBE stages run for which change (BrotherSBE ships no such logic), and the request to a Bitbucket admin for a merge check bound to the SBE build status key.

Three agent prerequisites that will bite on day one: python3 at 3.9 or newer on the build agent (a .NET SDK image will not have it, so either the image changes or the SBE stages route to a dedicated agent label), a non-shallow clone with tags because the approval gate reads commit trailers and signatures, and a decision about what happens on a T0 change. That last one is his work, not the tool's: BrotherSBE will happily FAIL a routine change if the pipeline asks it for a dossier that a T0 change never owed. Honest cost: this is a second hat on a person who is already the bottleneck, and the first month costs him time before it saves anyone any.

Two corrections to any stronger claim. First, the detector reads PATH NAMES, not code: a queue contract change made inside a .NET service whose path carries none of those words is not detected at all, and on this estate a lot of the real coupling lives in C# that the detector never sees and the linter cannot scan. Second, requiring a 00-intake.json on every change would be pure ceremony, because most changes here are T0 and owe nothing. The intake is worth writing only when the detector proposes a floor above T0, and BrotherSBE does not make that call for you: someone has to write the pipeline branch that only demands an intake when the floor is raised.

roles.role: Head of Project, holder of the manual production approval
roles.owns: Accountable for the Jenkins input step that promotes Staging to Production, with its one hour timeout.
roles.artifact_they_produce: The Proceed click. Today that is the whole artifact, and it stays the whole artifact.
roles.artifact_they_consume: An evidence pack written to the build description by a stage that runs immediately before input: bin/sbe status . --team plus, when the change carried a dossier, the four hard gate verdicts re-run against the release commit.
roles.what_changes_for_them: Inside the hour he reads verdicts bound to the exact commit being promoted instead of a recollection from a chat thread. Four things that do not change and must not be sold as if they did. BrotherSBE never learns the click happened. The Jenkins input approval and the SBE approval gate are two different approvals and describing them as one is the single most dangerous sentence available here. The gate verdicts in the pack are the same verdicts that already passed at PR time, so re-running them proves the commit is unchanged, not that Staging behaved. And for a T0 change, which is most of them, the pack is close to empty and he is back to reading a build number, so the honest benefit here is narrow: it applies to the T2 and T3 promotions, and it is thin on everything else.

roles.role: QC engineers (three, offshore)
roles.owns: Responsible for verification on Staging and Pre-Production before the promotion gate.
roles.artifact_they_produce: For checks that are a COMMAND, a ran-receipt generated by wrapping that command in bin/sbe evidence run. For a reconciliation with a figure in it, a numbers manifest with a pinned snapshot id and a second derivation whose text differs. For everything they do by hand, nothing.
roles.artifact_they_consume: The gate verdicts naming which receipts were missing, and the printed scope of the change under test.
roles.what_changes_for_them: This group's benefit is THIN and should be presented that way. An automated suite or a SQL reconciliation run through bin/sbe evidence run stops being a screenshot in a chat thread and becomes a receipt carrying an exit code, a duration and output digests. But three offshore QC engineers doing exploratory testing across a mobile app, a shop web app and a portal web app produce almost nothing this can receipt: BrotherSBE cannot observe a human clicking through the shop, has no view of a test management tool, and a receipt is only ever proof that a command ran, never that a person looked. It also has no opinion on visual design, accessibility or content quality, which is a large fraction of what gets checked on those three front ends. The one operational thing they will hit in week one is a cost, not a gain: a receipt made on a feature branch tip FAILs at the merge commit, and this repo enforces linear history, so receipts have to be regenerated by the pipeline on the post-rebase head.

roles.role: Night Dev BE and Night Dev FE (the timezone boundary the release path crosses)
roles.owns: Responsible for the commits that land while Tokyo is asleep and that Tokyo inherits at 10:00 JST.
roles.artifact_they_produce: Only if they work inside a Claude Code session: a task registry record opened before writing that declares the paths they will touch, plus a handover prepared for a named receiver. Outside such a session, nothing exists to produce.
roles.artifact_they_consume: The fence list, and the postcondition at bin/sbe work check <task-id>, which diffs what was written against what was declared.
roles.what_changes_for_them: If and only if they are running Claude Code, they declare write scope at 02:00 JST before writing rather than explaining it at 10:00, and the Tokyo reviewer opens a machine-checked diff against that declaration. That conditional is the whole answer. The fence governs writers who register, inside a Claude Code session, and nothing in Jenkins can create a declaration retroactively for a developer who never opened one. Do not put bin/sbe work check in the blocking path: a developer who never registered gives it nothing to read, and NO-DATA is never a pass, so a strict blocking stage would fail the build of everyone who has not opted in. Keep it advisory, and treat the timezone benefit as real only for the people actually using the tool.

today_without_sbe: Jenkins green means the tests this repo happens to have ran. Nothing binds a check result to the commit it was run against, so a SQL Server change whose reconciliation query never executed still reaches the merge check with a green build key.

The Bitbucket rule of minimum two reviewers with Tech Lead approval enforces a count of clicks. Whether your instance also stops an author approving their own pull request depends on the Bitbucket edition and its settings, so confirm it rather than assuming either way. What no merge check can tell you is whether anything was verified: it cannot see whether a reverse migration exists, and it cannot distinguish a review that read the diff from one that did not.

The one hour production approval timeout runs against no packaged evidence. The approver reads a build number, a Sentry release tag and whatever is in the chat thread. If the hour lapses the deploy re-queues and the same thin basis is presented again.

Offshore developers push at 02:00 JST and Tokyo reviews at 10:00. There is no record of what was declared before the work started, so scope drift is discovered at Staging, in Tokyo hours, against code written by someone who is now asleep.

Migration reversibility on SQL Server is a claim in a ticket comment. The reverse is rarely rehearsed against a restored copy, and row counts before and after are not recorded, so the schema half of the DR posture is untested even though the infrastructure half is exercised.
Helm chart and values edits ride inside feature branches and get reviewed as YAML by application reviewers. Nothing raises the risk tier when a change touches charts/, k8s/ or the Jenkinsfile itself.

Sentry release tagging tells you which commit is live. It does not tell you what evidence backed the promotion of that commit, so an incident investigation starts from a commit and has nowhere to walk back to.

with_sbe.step: Stage 0, the stage that decides whether any of the rest should run at all. Most changes here are T0 and owe nothing, so the pipeline must cost them nothing
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe impact . --base origin/master (no --intake, no --strict), then a Jenkins when{} condition on the printed tier floor
with_sbe.who_does_it: Jenkins agent. The branching logic is written by the Full Stack lead: BrotherSBE ships no pipeline file, no Jenkins condition and no opinion about when to skip itself
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Ceremony on routine work, which is the fastest way to get the whole thing switched off. Without this stage a T0 bug fix gets asked for a dossier it never owed, the build goes red for a reason nobody accepts, and within a sprint someone adds a skip that never comes off.

with_sbe.step: Stage 1: check the SBE checkout matches the manifest that shipped with its pinned ref
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: sh scripts/verify-install.sh
with_sbe.who_does_it: Jenkins agent
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A half-updated or partially overwritten checkout of the checker producing verdicts nobody can attribute to a version. Be exact about its strength: it compares files on disk against a manifest that travels with those same files, in both directions. That catches drift and accident. It is not a defence against someone who edits the manifest too.

with_sbe.step: Stage 2: reconcile the diff against a declared tier, only for changes the detector floored above T0
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe impact . --base origin/master --intake design/<change>/00-intake.json --strict
with_sbe.who_does_it: Jenkins agent
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A change touching helm/, charts/, k8s/, kubernetes/, .tf, .tfvars, docker-compose, a Jenkinsfile, a production-config path or a path containing rabbitmq being declared T0. The detector proposes a floor from PATH NAMES and a declared tier below that floor exits nonzero. It reads no code, so a boundary change in a file whose path carries none of those words is invisible to it.

with_sbe.step: Stage 3: dossier completeness and plan validation, for T2 and T3 changes only
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe design design/<change> --strict, then bin/sbe plan design/<change>
with_sbe.who_does_it: Jenkins agent
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A T2 or T3 change reaching the merge check with a shipped-template file still in place, an ADR with no genuine rejected alternative and no flip condition, a data model where an entity names no system of record, or an empty plan. It checks that the artifacts exist and are structurally complete. It cannot check that they are true, and a dossier written after the code was finished passes exactly the same.

with_sbe.step: Stage 4: the four hard gates, with the keyring imported first, for changes that carry a dossier
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: gpg --import from the approver public keyring, then bin/sbe gate design/<change> --strict
with_sbe.who_does_it: Jenkins agent. The keyring is fetched by the existing Vault step and imported in the same stage
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: numbers: a figure with no pinned snapshot or no textually distinct second derivation. migration: a forward with no rehearsed reverse against a restored copy, no rehearsal id, or row counts that do not match. approval: a typed name with no signature, and self-approval, because the Approved-by identity is compared against the commit author and committer. ran: a check that never executed. Without the imported keys git reports %G? = E, every signed approval reads NO-DATA, and under --strict that is a nonzero exit and never a pass. What it does NOT do: notice that a change needed an approval nobody declared.

with_sbe.step: Stage 5: silent-failure lints. The only SBE stage most pull requests here will ever feel
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe score --strict .
with_sbe.who_does_it: Jenkins agent, running in parallel with the existing SonarQube stage and not replacing it
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Bare except, except-then-pass, a discarded subprocess result, a conflict-skipping upsert, force-try. Scope caveat that decides how you present this: tools/sbe_score.py pins the scannable set to .py .sql .swift .rb .js .ts .go and .cs is not in it, so on six .NET microservices this reaches the SQL, the front end TypeScript and the scripts, and nothing else. SonarQube stays the primary code-quality gate for C#.

with_sbe.step: Stage 6: generate evidence inside the pipeline so receipts come from a run and carry the CI label
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: SBE_CI_RUN_ID=$BUILD_TAG bin/sbe evidence run --out <path outside the working tree> --covers <paths> -- <the real check command>, then bin/sbe evidence verify per receipt
with_sbe.who_does_it: Jenkins agent. QC engineers name which command counts as the check
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A receipt typed to satisfy the schema. The wrapper executes the command, so duration, exit code and output digests come from an execution. Two operational rules that are not optional: write receipts OUTSIDE the tree they cover, because a receipt written into that tree makes it dirty and demotes the next receipt to advisory, and generate on the head the merge will use, because a pre-rebase receipt FAILs at a rebased head.

with_sbe.step: Stage 7: convergence against the approved dossier, for changes that have one
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe converge design/<change> --base origin/master --head $GIT_COMMIT
with_sbe.who_does_it: Jenkins agent
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: The change that quietly grew between design approval and merge. It compares scope, contract shapes, data model, architecture and verification, there is no force flag, and it names every dimension it had nothing to read. It compares STRUCTURES, not intent, and it has nothing to say about a change that never carried a dossier.

with_sbe.step: Stage 8: publish the human-readable summary to the build
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe status . --team, written to currentBuild.description
with_sbe.who_does_it: Jenkins agent
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A reviewer in Tokyo reconstructing an offshore change from the diff alone. The summary is blocker-first and carries a basis field per finding stating what the verdict rests on. It is an input to the two human reviewers this repo already requires, and it replaces neither of them.

with_sbe.step: Stage 9, CD pipeline on merge to master: assemble the promotion pack immediately before the input step
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: Re-run bin/sbe gate design/<change> --strict and bin/sbe status . --team against the release commit, archive as a build artifact, write the summary into the build description, then the existing input step with its one hour timeout
with_sbe.who_does_it: Jenkins CD job. The Head of Project reads it and clicks
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: An approval given inside a one hour window on no stated basis, for the T2 and T3 promotions that carry a dossier. Be exact: BrotherSBE assembles the pack and exits. It does not perform the click, cannot be the approver, never learns the promotion happened, and for a T0 promotion the pack adds nothing the approver did not already have.

with_sbe.step: Advisory to enforcing, and where the stop actually happens
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: Phase 1: every SBE stage wrapped in catchError(buildResult: 'SUCCESS', stageResult: 'UNSTABLE'), starting with score alone. Phase 2: unwrap stage by stage, in the order score, impact, design and gate, converge. Then a Bitbucket merge check of the class 'minimum successful builds on the source commit' bound to the SBE build status key
with_sbe.who_does_it: Full Stack lead removes the wrappers. A Bitbucket admin configures the merge check. Nobody at BrotherSBE does either
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Betting the merge queue on a checker that has never run against this codebase. Never soften a stage with || true or set +e: a discarded exit code is the exact defect class the silent-failure linter exists to catch, and it would also hide NO-DATA, which is never a pass. The stop is performed by Jenkins failing a build and Bitbucket refusing a merge. BrotherSBE only exits a code.

integration_points.system: Running bin/sbe locally, in a Claude Code session, against a checkout
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Every command works on a developer machine with no pipeline, no server and no credential of any kind
integration_points.mechanism: python3 3.9 or newer, standard library only, no package index. This is the only thing on this list that genuinely works the day it is installed, and it is where the advisory phase should start: run it by hand against real branches for a sprint before any Jenkinsfile is touched.
integration_points.confidence: ships today

integration_points.system: Jenkins CI, the PR pipeline (triggered on PR open and on push to the PR branch)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Added stages between checkout and the existing SonarQube and Trivy stages, all calling bin/sbe and all returning that tool's own exit code
integration_points.mechanism: Declarative stages the team writes in the existing multibranch Jenkinsfile, plus the when{} logic that keeps T0 changes free of all of it. Three prerequisites: python3 at 3.9 or newer on the agent image, a non-shallow clone with full history and tags because the approval gate reads trailers and signatures, and the approver public keys imported before the gate stage. BrotherSBE ships no Jenkinsfile, no shared library, no stage template and no skip logic.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Jenkins CD, the production approval input with its one hour timeout
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: One stage immediately before the input step that regenerates the gate verdicts and the team status against the release commit
integration_points.mechanism: archiveArtifacts of the verdict output plus currentBuild.description carrying the blocker-first summary, so the pack sits on the same page as the Proceed button. BrotherSBE never calls the input step, never approves, never deploys and never observes the outcome.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Bitbucket branch permissions and merge checks
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Nothing. BrotherSBE ships no branch protection, no merge check config and no pipeline file for this host. It exits nonzero and stops there
integration_points.mechanism: The team binds a merge check of the class 'minimum number of successful builds on the source commit' to the SBE build status key Jenkins posts. What that check CAN require: a green named build key on the exact source commit, a minimum approval count, default reviewer approval, no unresolved tasks, no force push, linear history, branch up to date. What it CANNOT do: read the difference between FAIL and NO-DATA (it sees one red or green key, which is why --strict must make NO-DATA exit nonzero), require that a named evidence artifact exists, compare an approver identity against the commit author, or say anything about which files changed. Check names differ between Bitbucket Cloud and Data Center, so confirm them in your own instance.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Bitbucket pull request approvals, read programmatically
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Nowhere. src/brothersbe/prverify.py hardcodes https://api.github.com and discovers its token through GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or gh auth token. There is no Bitbucket client anywhere in the codebase
integration_points.mechanism: Step 9 of the shipped CI order does not exist on this estate. The two substitutes: standardise on a signed Approved-by trailer, which the approval gate verifies LOCALLY via git and therefore works on any host including Bitbucket, or write your own Jenkins stage that queries the Bitbucket REST API for the PR's approvals and fails the build. BrotherSBE ships no such stage, and it will not resolve a Reviewed-in id against Bitbucket either.
integration_points.confidence: not possible

integration_points.system: sbe protections, the command that reports whether the repository protects its own control plane
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Do not run it here. src/brothersbe/protections.py shells out to gh api for the branch ruleset, and its local leg reads CODEOWNERS from .github/CODEOWNERS, CODEOWNERS or docs/CODEOWNERS
integration_points.mechanism: Both legs are GitHub-shaped. The network leg cannot reach Bitbucket at all. Worse for a Bitbucket repo, a missing or non-covering CODEOWNERS file is deliberately a FAIL rather than a NO-DATA, so this command will fail permanently on an estate that correctly has no CODEOWNERS file. The adoption kit's CODEOWNERS example also ships the literal placeholder @REPLACE-ME and protects nothing. Keep this command out of the pipeline and out of the pitch.
integration_points.confidence: not possible

integration_points.system: HashiCorp Vault
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: The approval gate stage, which needs the approvers' GPG or SSH public keys in the agent keyring before git can report %G? = G
integration_points.mechanism: Store the approver public keyring at a Vault KV path, fetch it with the same withCredentials or Vault plugin step the deploy already uses, gpg --import at the start of the gate stage. Say internally that public keys are not secret: Vault here is central distribution and rotation, not confidentiality. BrotherSBE never reads Vault, never authenticates to anything and holds no credential.
integration_points.confidence: needs the team to wire it

integration_points.system: Helm charts, Terraform and EKS across Development (Osaka), Staging, Pre-Production and Production (Tokyo)
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: src/brothersbe/impact.py classes helm/, charts/, k8s/, kubernetes/, .tf, .tfvars, docker-compose and prod or production path segments as boundary or sensitive, which raises the tier floor
integration_points.mechanism: Path-name regex, evaluated only when someone runs sbe impact, which on this estate means only once a Jenkins stage exists to call it. The regex needs no work. The stage does. And that is the whole of the integration: BrotherSBE never runs helm, never runs kubectl, never reads a cluster, and has no idea what is deployed in either region. A chart is classified by where its file sits, not by what it does.

integration_points.system: RabbitMQ and the five queue processors
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: The queue-config detector matches any path containing kafka, rabbitmq, sqs, pubsub or kinesis and classes it as an asynchronous boundary between systems
integration_points.mechanism: Path-name regex only, and again only once a Jenkins stage calls sbe impact. A CartSync or ProductSync change under a rabbitmq path raises the floor and forces the consumer question at PR open. A queue contract change made inside a C# service whose path carries none of those words is not detected, and on this estate that is the likelier place for it to live.

integration_points.system: Pimcore and Strapi as systems of record for product master data and content
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Only as words a human types into a data model file. BrotherSBE reads no PIM schema, no CMS content type, no sync job and no field mapping
integration_points.mechanism: The data model check verifies that every entity NAMES a system of record and every relationship carries a cardinality. It cannot verify that the named system is the real one, and it will pass a document that says Strapi where the truth is Pimcore. Useful as a forcing question for the Integration Manager, worthless as a control.

integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Nowhere. They run in the same pipeline and share no data in either direction
integration_points.mechanism: There is no integration to build and none is wanted. The silent-failure linter does not cover .cs, so SonarQube stays the primary code-quality gate for the microservices. BrotherSBE scans no images and performs no secret detection, so Trivy and Gitleaks are untouched. Presenting these as integrated, or the linter as backend coverage, would be the overpromise.

integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: No integration exists with any of them. BrotherSBE reads no telemetry of any kind

Nothing computes or enforces this, and there is no post-deploy verification, no error-budget awareness and no rollback trigger anywhere in the tool.

integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Every design stage, plus the gates and convergence, read it from the checkout
integration_points.mechanism: Dossiers live under design/ in the repository, versioned with the code and reviewed in the same pull request. Reading them works today. Getting them written, kept current and reviewed is a team habit no tool supplies. Leave SBE_DOSSIER_ROOT UNSET on these repos: a declared root holding no dossier is a FAIL by design, and on an estate where T0 work and dossier work mix that setting turns every routine change red.

integration_points.system: The DR posture: Osaka active-passive, semi-automated failover under four hours, DNS redirect, daily encrypted backups
integration_points.where_sbe_touches_it: Only obliquely, through the migration gate's requirement that a reverse ran against a restored copy

BrotherSBE does not test failover, does not measure the four hour target, does not touch DNS, does not check a backup, and the restored copy in its receipt is not the DR replica unless the team chose to make it so.

release_points: Before any pipeline change at all: bin/sbe run by hand against real branches on a laptop. This is the only release point that costs nothing to reach and it should absorb the first sprint or two.

PR open and every push to the PR branch: the Jenkins CI job runs the SBE stages advisory-first, then enforcing, starting with score alone. This is the only point where a merge is actually stopped, and Bitbucket does the stopping, not BrotherSBE.

The T0 path through PR open, which is most changes: impact prints a floor of T0, the dossier stages are skipped, score runs, and nothing else is owed. If a T0 change ever goes red for a missing artifact, the pipeline is wired wrong.
Merge to master: gates and receipts re-run against the merge commit, because both are commit-bound and a pre-rebase receipt FAILs at a rebased head under this repo's linear history rule.

Auto-deploy to Staging: verification receipts are generated by the pipeline with SBE_CI_RUN_ID set to $BUILD_TAG so they read CI-CLAIMED rather than LOCAL-ADVISORY. That label states provenance, it does not authenticate it.

Pre-Production: the natural place to run and record the migration forward and reverse rehearsal against a restored copy, since Pre-Prod shares the Tokyo EKS with dedicated node groups and can carry a restored database.

The manual production approval input, one hour timeout: the evidence pack is written to the build description immediately before it. BrotherSBE assembles, a human clicks, and BrotherSBE never learns what was clicked.
Rolling update to Production: no BrotherSBE presence. It never deploys, never rolls back, and observes nothing after promotion.

Hotfix/xxx under incident pressure at 03:00 JST: no incident mode exists. Decide in advance which stages a hotfix runs, because a gate that blocks an incident fix will be waived once and then removed.
DR failover rehearsal (Osaka): no BrotherSBE presence at all.
honest_limits_for_this_group: BrotherSBE never deploys, never merges, never approves. It runs a check and exits a code. Every stop in this design is performed by Jenkins failing a build and Bitbucket refusing a merge. Phrased once for leadership: it can make a bad change loud, it cannot make a bad change impossible.

It replaces no human review, no standup and no decision. The two-reviewer rule and the Tech Lead approval stay exactly as they are, the promotion decision stays with the Head of Project, and every verdict SBE prints is an input to a person, never a substitute for one.

Most changes on this estate are T0 and owe nothing. If the pipeline is built to demand a dossier per change, the team will produce empty dossiers to get green and the control degrades into form-filling. Designing the T0 path to cost zero is a prerequisite, not a nicety, and BrotherSBE ships no logic that does it for you.

bin/sbe pr verify is GitHub-only: src/brothersbe/prverify.py hardcodes https://api.github.com and finds its token through GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or gh auth token. On Bitbucket that step does not exist, and nothing here reads a Bitbucket approval, a Bitbucket merge check state or Bitbucket branch permissions.

bin/sbe protections is also GitHub-only and is actively harmful here: it calls gh api for the ruleset and treats a missing CODEOWNERS as a FAIL rather than NO-DATA, so on a Bitbucket repo with no CODEOWNERS file it fails permanently for a reason that is not a defect. Keep it out of the pipeline.

Nothing detects that a change NEEDED an approval. The gate verifies an approval that was declared. A T3 change whose author never wrote an APPROVAL file gets NO-DATA, which blocks under --strict, but only if there is a dossier being checked at all. No dossier means no gate, and nothing notices the absence.

The signed approval path needs the approvers' public keys on every Jenkins agent that runs the gate. With no keyring git reports %G? = E and every signed approval is NO-DATA. A valid signature whose key matches nothing the host trusts (%G? = U, the default for a self-generated SSH signing key) is also NO-DATA, never an approval. The keyless Reviewed-in: <id> path proves only that a non-vacuous string was typed into a commit message, and BrotherSBE resolves it against nothing.

The silent-failure linter's scannable set is pinned in tools/sbe_score.py to .py .sql .swift .rb .js .ts .go. .cs is not in it. On an estate whose core is six .NET microservices, most of the application code is invisible to it. Do not present it as backend coverage.

The numbers gate proves two derivations differ in TEXT. It does not prove they are independent. Two queries over the same broken SQL Server view, or two reads of the same stale Elasticsearch index, both pass.

The migration gate's rehearsal id is a string. Nothing resolves it against a Jenkins build number, a restore log or any job system. It is a pointer for a human, and if you want it to be a control you write that resolver yourself.

SBE_CI_RUN_ID=$BUILD_TAG produces a CI-CLAIMED receipt. The label states where the value came from, it does not authenticate it, and any process can export the same variable. Its worth is that the Jenkinsfile is a thing humans control through the merge path.

Receipts are commit-bound and strict about it. A pre-rebase receipt FAILs at the merge commit, and a covered file rewritten after the run (a checkout, a formatter, even with identical bytes) invalidates it. Plan on the pipeline regenerating receipts on the post-rebase head. Also keep receipts outside the tree they cover, because a receipt written into that tree makes it dirty and demotes the next one to advisory.

Nothing gives manual or exploratory QA a receipt. A receipt is proof a command ran. Three QC engineers clicking through a mobile app, a shop web app and a portal web app produce almost nothing this tool can see, and it has no opinion on visual design, accessibility, content quality or copy, which is a large part of what those three surfaces need checked.

The impact detectors read PATH NAMES, not code. A boundary or queue contract change made inside a C# service whose path carries none of the trigger words is not detected, and the linter cannot read that file either. On this estate the two blind spots overlap.

sbe instruction-surface watches CLAUDE.md, .claude/**, .mcp.json, .claude-plugin/**, hooks/**, agents/*.md, skills/*/SKILL.md, CODEOWNERS and .github/workflows/**. It does NOT watch Jenkinsfile or bitbucket-pipelines.yml, so the pipeline definition is not an authority surface to that check. sbe impact does class a Jenkinsfile change as a boundary, which is a weaker signal, and the real protection for that file is a Bitbucket branch permission the team sets.

BrotherSBE ships no CODEOWNERS, no branch protection, no merge checks and no CI configuration for this host. Its own protections report calls branch protection state UNVERIFIABLE-HERE, unconditionally.

Nothing reads Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch, ELK, Sentry or Alertmanager. There is no post-deploy verification of any kind, no error-budget awareness and no automatic rollback trigger. Once the rolling update starts, BrotherSBE has nothing to say.
Nothing tests the Osaka failover, the sub four hour target, the DNS redirect or the daily encrypted backups. The migration gate's restored copy is a restore your team performed, not the DR replica.

The spine, meaning design before verification and install the check before writing the work, is a stated discipline. No tool computes it and Jenkins cannot enforce an ordering that spans days. A complete dossier written after the code will pass every gate.

No measurement exists for what these stages cost in wall clock on this repository. The PR pipeline already runs build, tests, Gitleaks, SonarQube, Trivy and packaging. Added minutes on every push are unverified until the advisory phase measures them, and a slow merge path gets bypassed.

A gate exemption (.sbe-exempt) is visible, never silent, and every waived line is printed on every run. It is still an exemption. A waiver is not a pass, and if it stops being read it stops being a control.

There is no incident mode. A hotfix at 03:00 JST hits the same gates as a planned change, which is exactly when a blocking gate gets waived once and then quietly deleted. Decide the hotfix path before enforcement, not during an outage.

Every threshold shipped was measured on ONE estate, and the full CI order has run end to end only against that project's own fixtures. No external organisation has executed it. Adopting here makes this team the second data point, which is why the advisory phase is not optional: run it non-blocking for a real sprint or two, read the false positives against this codebase's own idioms, and decide from real output whether it can carry a merge queue.

This group is not staffed as a distinct platform team. The Jenkinsfile, the Helm charts and the Bitbucket configuration are a second hat worn by the Full Stack lead and the Integration Manager, both in Japan, while the pipeline runs code written offshore overnight. Every stage added to the merge path is maintenance for two people who are already the bottleneck, and the first month costs them time before it saves any.

checked.group: Sales, Onboarding and Customer Success, Marketing (Sales Manager, Account Manager, Operations Consultants, two CS Specialists, Onboarding Specialist, Marketing lead)

roles.owns: Responsible for lifecycle and campaign requests, including ones that move customer data into third-party tools.
roles.artifact_they_produce: Spoken answers to the five intake questions, which a BA types into the interactive prompt. The answers are self-declared and nothing at that moment checks them.

today_without_sbe: An Operations Consultant reports wrong prices for one outlet. Nobody establishes whether the fault is Pimcore master data, the Product service, the ProductSync queue processor or a stale Elasticsearch index. The question crosses to the offshore team and returns as a clarifying question the next Japan morning, and pricing questions typically take two or three such loops.

A CS Specialist has no artifact answering whether a fix is live in production. The people who know include a Night Dev BE and a Night Dev FE who are offline during Japan business hours, so CS either guesses from a Sentry release note they cannot interpret or tells the customer to wait.

A request to push a customer segment into Klaviyo moves personal data across a service boundary to a third party, and enters the backlog with the same ceremony as a banner copy change. Nothing in the current intake asks the personal-data question.

Requests arrive with no non-goals. A small pricing display fix is scoped by whoever picks it up and grows into a change in the Cart service. The two reviewers plus Tech Lead approval that this now needs were never budgeted.

Sales quotes a date from the Staging auto-deploy without knowing Production needs a manual approval on a one hour timeout, a window that often opens after Japan has gone home and closes before the offshore team starts.

The Onboarding Specialist hits a half-created retailer account and cannot tell whether the customer record is mastered in Pimcore, the Customer service or Cognito. No document states the system of record.
Pre-production acceptance is a subjective walkthrough with no written criteria, so a rejection is a feeling rather than a named failed condition.

with_sbe.step: Score the request first, before deciding how much writing it owes. Five questions, asked out loud, answered by the commercial requester because they are the only person who knows whether it touches money, partner data, personal data, production state, or is reversible within an hour.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe intake <dossier-directory>, an interactive terminal prompt run by a BA or engineer, writing 00-intake.json. It fixes the artifacts owed: T0 none, T1 only 01-purpose.md, T2 six files, T3 all seven.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Business Analyst runs the prompt and types the answers. Nobody in this group touches a terminal.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: Both failure directions. It stops a Klaviyo or pricing change being worked at T0 ceremony, and equally it stops the rest of the group's traffic being buried in artifacts it does not owe. Its own weakness is stated in the plugin: the tier is computed from answers, not from the change.

with_sbe.step: For T1 and above only, the requester's words become 01-purpose.md: problem without a solution in it, users and their workaround, observable success criteria, non-goals, blast radius. At T0 this step is skipped entirely and no dossier directory is created.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: templates/dossier/01-purpose.md, filled and committed on the feature branch. A text file, not a command.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Sales Manager, Account Manager, CS Specialist or Marketing lead supplies the words. The BA transcribes and commits.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: One clarification round trip per request that would otherwise be answered in offshore hours. The prevention is human: the design check verifies only that the file is not the shipped template and not empty or filled with TODO. A confidently written vague brief passes.

with_sbe.step: For T2 and T3 work, each success criterion becomes a row in the verification plan: the claim on the left, the check that proves it on the right, and when it runs. A CS Specialist or Ops Consultant reads the left column and says whether it restates the customer symptom.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: templates/dossier/07-verification.md, the claim-to-check table.
with_sbe.who_does_it: BA and engineer write the rows. The commercial requester confirms the left column. No tool validates the pairing.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A fix that passes its tests while the reported symptom persists, on the subset of work that is T2 or above. It prevents nothing on T0 and T1 work, which is most tickets.

with_sbe.step: Pre-production acceptance on T2 and T3 changes is walked against that table, and a rejection names the failing row instead of expressing a feeling.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: 07-verification.md used as the acceptance script, plus the Non-goals text as the scope boundary.
with_sbe.who_does_it: Operations Consultants and the Account Manager. Requires that somebody first published the file where a person without a Bitbucket account can read it.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: An ambiguous rejection that costs another handover cycle. It does not prevent scope creep: Non-goals is unenforced prose that a person has to notice and quote.

with_sbe.step: Run the diff reconciliation on the branch before review, so a change that was declared T0 but touches a contract, a schema or an infrastructure path is raised as a floor.
with_sbe.command_or_artifact: bin/sbe impact, which converts detector hits from the git diff into the same five intake answers and recomputes the tier.
with_sbe.who_does_it: An engineer or BA runs it. This group never sees the command, only the consequence when a request they scored low comes back needing more.
with_sbe.what_it_prevents: A segment sync or pricing change being declared T0 and staying there unchallenged. Its limits are explicit in the tool: it can only raise a tier, never lower one, it cannot see how many consumers break, and a service call added inside existing code is invisible to a path-based detector. A Klaviyo sync written entirely inside existing service code may trip nothing at all.
