release_points: Request intake, before any environment. The only point where this group is the primary author, and the only one worth their time. A rewrite here costs a conversation. Note that for T0 requests the output of this point is a scored intake file and nothing else.

Development (Osaka, isolated EKS): no touchpoint for this group, and it should stay that way. The environment is isolated and not representative, so pulling commercial staff in produces false confidence.

Staging (Tokyo EKS, auto-deployed by the team's existing Jenkins pipeline): the first place a CS or Onboarding Specialist can check a criterion against something running, inside Japan hours. BrotherSBE contributes nothing to this deploy; the automation is already the team's.

Pre-Production (Tokyo EKS, dedicated node groups): acceptance by Operations Consultants and the Account Manager, walked against the claim-to-check table on T2 and T3 changes only. On T0 and T1 changes there is no table and acceptance is unchanged.

Production (manual approval, one hour timeout, rolling update): the gate this group cares about and the one BrotherSBE touches least. It never gets apply rights, cannot deploy, cannot approve, cannot merge. It drafts a command and its rollback for a human to run. The approval gate can only verify that a declared approval trailer names somebody other than the author; nothing detects that an approval was needed and skipped, and nothing here reports whether the release actually went out.
honest_limits_for_this_group: T0 owes nothing, and T0 is the common case. Most of what this group asks for produces one scored intake file and no dossier. Any description of their new working week that assumes a purpose brief per request is describing the exception, not the rule.

T1 owes exactly one file, 01-purpose.md. The claim-to-check table and the data model, the two artifacts this group would benefit from most, are required only at T2 and T3. For the Ops Consultants and the Onboarding Specialist that means the promised benefit arrives on a minority of tickets.

Nobody in this group opens a terminal, and nothing in the design suggests they should. Every command named here is run by a BA, a PM or an engineer, and the intake tool is an interactive prompt somebody else types their answers into.

BrotherSBE enforces nothing on Bitbucket or Jenkins. It ships no branch protection, no merge check and no pipeline configuration for either. The consumer integration that does exist in the repository is written for GitHub Actions and is unusable on this team's host. The gates are also advisory unless run with the strict flag, so a wired pipeline can run them and block nothing.

No receipt describes production. Receipts observe a command running in CI, and production here is a separate manual approval after that. A CS Specialist asking whether a fix is live in production cannot get that answer from BrotherSBE, today or after wiring.

The receipts BrotherSBE mints by default cover its own design, gate and score runs. A receipt about the customer's symptom exists only if an engineer writes that check and the team wires and publishes it. A green receipt beside a still-broken customer is the honest failure mode.

The half of this group's working life that generates the most tickets is completely uncovered. Product data in Pimcore, content in Strapi, campaigns in Klaviyo, voucher rules in Voucherify, deep links in Branch.io: none of it passes through a diff, so none of it gets a design phase, a gate, a linter or a receipt. Say this on day one, not after a miss.

The tier is computed from answers, not from the change. The diff reconciliation can raise a tier after code exists, but it can only raise, it cannot count consumers, and it misses a boundary crossing written inside existing code. A confident no to the personal-data question stands unchallenged until somebody notices.

A well-formed purpose brief is not a true one. The design check tests that the file is not the shipped template, is not empty or all-TODO, and shares subject words with the rest of its dossier. At T1, where 01-purpose.md is the only file, there is nothing to compare it against and the coherence rule is not measured at all. It never tests whether a success criterion is observable or whether it is what the customer wanted.

Nothing detects that a change needed commercial or business approval. The approval gate verifies a declared, host-verified trailer and rejects self-approval. A change that quietly skipped commercial sign-off is invisible to it.

Where a commercial request produces a number (a price, a discount, a rebate, a volume commitment), the numbers gate proves only that two derivations differ in text. It does not prove they are independent. Two queries over the same broken view both pass and the number is still wrong. This is a live exposure for pricing and rebate work.

It replaces no human. Not a reviewer, not a standup, not a decision, not the timezone handover. Two reviewers and Tech Lead approval are still required by the team's own branch policy, and the plugin neither performs nor substitutes for any of them.

It has no opinion on visual design, accessibility, content quality or copy, which removes most of the Marketing lead's surface. The honest position for this group is that direct gain is thin: one file some of them help write, on a minority of changes, and one file most of them cannot currently open. The indirect gain is the real one, and it is worth stating plainly rather than dressing up: ambiguity gets a named place to die upstream, in Japan hours, before it costs a day of offshore round trip.
Every threshold shipped was measured on one estate, not this one. Expect the tier boundaries and the check set to need refitting, and expect that refitting to be argued about.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 1. Commercial request arrives. A liquor retailer sees the wrong case pack price on the shop web app. The Account Manager and an Operations Consultant establish segment (retailer, not hospitality), surface (shop web app and the portal), and the workaround. The fix is a change to a price-bearing field on the Pimcore product class: it is retyped and its unit semantics change, and Order Service, Cart Service and the Elasticsearch search index all read it.
end_to_end_flow.who: Account Manager and Operations Consultant, with a CS Specialist holding the ticket
end_to_end_flow.system: Ticket tracker, chat, a screenshot. BrotherSBE has no tracker integration of any kind and cannot see this.
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: None. Nothing here is a BrotherSBE surface. The only discipline available is a team convention that the request states an outcome and a blast radius before a BA picks it up.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: A ticket description in the tracker, plus the words that will later be transcribed into 01-purpose.md. The link from this ticket to design/pim-case-price-field/ is a line a BA types by hand, and if they stop typing it the chain breaks with no signal.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 2. Score the change before deciding how much writing it owes. The BA runs the five-question intake with the Marketing lead and Account Manager in the room, because they are the only people who know it touches money. Answering yes to the money question computes T3, which owes all seven artifacts. Answering no would compute T0, which owes nothing, and nothing at this moment contradicts a wrong answer.
end_to_end_flow.who: Business Analyst (lead), answers supplied out loud by the commercial requester
end_to_end_flow.system: A terminal on the BA's laptop. Nobody in the commercial group touches it.
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: python3 tools/sbe_intake.py design/pim-case-price-field, writing 00-intake.json with the five answers and the computed tier. Verified in tools/sbe_intake.py: REQUIRED["T0"] is the empty list, T1 is ["01"], T2 is ["01","02","03","05","06","07"], T3 is all seven.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: design/pim-case-price-field/00-intake.json, committed on a feature branch. This is the file every later stage reads to know what is owed.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 3. Write purpose, process and verification in Tokyo hours, while the people who know the intent are awake. The process artifact names an actor, a trigger and an exception path per step, and the Designer names the exception states across the mobile app, shop web app and portal: stale price, partial ProductSync, Elasticsearch index behind the database, Voucherify unreachable when a voucher stacks on the contract price. The verification artifact pairs every claim with the check that proves it, written before any code exists.
end_to_end_flow.who: Business Analyst (lead), with the Designer on the exception states and QC on the claim-to-check rows
end_to_end_flow.system: Markdown files in the repository under design/pim-case-price-field/
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: 01-purpose.md, 02-process.md, 07-verification.md. Be exact about what is checked: nothing reads any of these three for content. The design checks verify only that the file is present and is not still the shipped template. A one-sentence purpose brief passes.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: Three markdown files in the branch. Contractor Operations Consultants and CS Specialists typically have no Bitbucket account, so somebody must publish a readable copy or the people whose words are in the file cannot open it.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 4. Write down which store owns the field, once, for real. Pimcore is system of record for product master data. The SQL Server tables in Product Service are a replica written by ProductSync. Elasticsearch is a derived index. Strapi is system of record for editorial copy only, not for price. Every relationship carries a cardinality, including product variant to SKU to retailer contract price list, which is many-to-many on this business and gets implemented as one-to-many by whoever writes the sync first. One ADR records why Pimcore and not the Product service, with two distinct rejected alternatives and a flip condition.
end_to_end_flow.who: Integration Manager, reviewed by the second Business Analyst
end_to_end_flow.system: Markdown in the repository. Nothing introspects Pimcore, Strapi, a queue binding or a .NET DTO.
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: 05-data-model.md and 03-adr.md, read by the datamodel and adr design checks. The datamodel check FAILs an entity with no system of record and a relationship with no cardinality. It checks that the field was FILLED, never that the answer is right: writing Strapi where the truth is Pimcore passes every check that ships.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: 05-data-model.md and 03-adr.md. This is the single highest-value artifact for this estate and it does not exist today, which is why the first hour of a catalogue incident goes to arguing which of five stores was supposed to be right.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 5. Make the field shape visible to git at all. This is the load-bearing prerequisite for the whole flow and the team builds it: a job that exports the Pimcore class definition to schemas/pimcore/Product.json and mirrors the Strapi content-type to schemas/strapi/<type>.json, committed to a branch. Without it, a field retyped and saved in the Pimcore admin UI produces no diff, no PR, no Jenkins run, no reviewer and no gate, and the first sign of trouble is a null in Elasticsearch seen by the night shift.
end_to_end_flow.who: PIM schema owner (a nominated Content Specialist role that does NOT exist today and the group must create), with a Development engineer owning the export job
end_to_end_flow.system: Pimcore, Bitbucket. BrotherSBE ships nothing that does this.
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: The exported definition committed under a path a detector matches. Verified in src/brothersbe/impact.py: the event-schema detector requires a DIRECTORY named event, events, schema or schemas, so Strapi's own content-types/<type>/schema.json does not match and must be mirrored. Nothing here has ever been run against a Pimcore installation.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: schemas/pimcore/Product.json in a Bitbucket pull request, so the shape half of the change traverses the same ladder as code. The data half, the Pimcore publish itself, still does not.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 6. Check the dossier before anything is handed offshore, and reconcile the declared tier against what the diff actually touched.
end_to_end_flow.who: Business Analyst (second seat) as refuter, or the PM
end_to_end_flow.system: A laptop, and later a Jenkins stage the team writes
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: python3 tools/sbe_design.py --strict design/pim-case-price-field (artifacts present, adr, datamodel, diagrams tracing to declared entities, placeholder) plus bin/sbe impact . --base origin/master --intake design/pim-case-price-field/00-intake.json --strict. The placeholder check naming a file still carrying the shipped template is the single line that stops a design gate becoming theatre. impact may raise a tier and may never lower one, it reads PATH NAMES not code, and its money detector matches pricing, discount and invoice but not the bare word price, so a file named PriceList.json raises to T2 and no further.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: A design verdict block and an impact verdict block. Neither blocks anything until a Jenkins stage and a Bitbucket merge check exist.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 7. Derive the plan and mint one work order per task for the night shift. The tasks split across the boundary: the Pimcore export and the ProductSync mapping, the Order Service and Cart Service DTO and its consumers, the Elasticsearch mapping and reindex, and the shop and portal front ends.
end_to_end_flow.who: PM for development, with the Full Stack lead
end_to_end_flow.system: Files in git. It schedules nothing and assigns nobody.
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: sbe plan writing 08-plan.json, then sbe work brief --plan 08-plan.json --task T04 --json per task: sorted keys, no timestamp, byte-identical across runs, refused rather than truncated past 8192 bytes, carrying scope, mustNotTouch, dependencies, acceptance, verificationCommands, knownConstraints, stopConditions, baselineCommit and requiredEvidenceKind.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: 08-plan.json plus one work brief JSON per task. stopConditions is the field that pays for itself across a timezone boundary: it names what to stop on rather than work around.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 8. THE TIMEZONE SEAM, outbound. Tokyo evening. Ownership transfers to the offshore night shift and does not move until a named human on the receiving side acknowledges by running the command themselves. Reject is a first-class outcome and leaves the outgoing owner as owner.
end_to_end_flow.who: PM or Full Stack lead prepares; the Night Dev BE and Night Dev FE acknowledge
end_to_end_flow.system: Files in git, read at a specific commit. Nothing notifies anybody.
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: sbe handover prepare design/pim-case-price-field --outgoing <identity> --receiver <identity>, writing 12-handover.json, then acknowledge or reject from the offshore side. Everything except the identities is derived: done, inFlight and notStarted from 08-plan.json against .sbe/tasks.json, active tasks with worktree and base commit, every worktree checked for uncommitted state, every evidence item tagged current, stale or unavailable. openQuestions, decisions and requiredAccess are written EMPTY and must be typed by a human.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: 12-handover.json with an acknowledgement recorded against a commit sha. It wakes nobody, notifies nobody and enforces no response time. It makes the state honest; it does not make the timezone smaller.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 9. Night shift implements against the dossier instead of a chat scrollback. The Night Dev BE changes the Order and Cart DTOs, the ProductSync and CartSync consumers and the SQL Server migration; the Night Dev FE changes the price display in the shop and portal apps. Evidence is minted by the runner that executed the command, never typed. A stop condition becomes a recorded stop and a written open question rather than eight hours of guessing.
end_to_end_flow.who: Night Dev BE and Night Dev FE, offshore, with no synchronous access to the BA who designed it
end_to_end_flow.system: Osaka isolated development EKS, restored SQL Server copy, local worktrees
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: bin/sbe evidence run --check <id> --kind gate --out <path outside the covered tree>, sealing base and head sha, redacted argv, exit code, duration and content digests of the declared covered paths; migration-receipt.json recording forward AND reverse both run against a restored copy, a rehearsal id and matching row counts. Receipts minted here are LOCAL-ADVISORY. sbe work start refuses a taken branch, a taken worktree or a re-opened task id, and never compares file scopes between two tasks, so overlap with the Japan front end developers is visible in a registry a human reads, not refused.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: Commits on sbe/pim-case-price-field/<taskId> branches, receipt JSON files, and migration-receipt.json. The silent-failure linter reads .py .sql .swift .rb .js .ts .go (verified at tools/sbe_score.py:655) so it reads the SQL and any plain .ts, and reads none of the .NET services, none of the queue processors and no .tsx or .jsx.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 10. THE TIMEZONE SEAM, inbound. 06:00 JST. The night shift prepares the return handover at a specific commit; Tokyo acknowledges or rejects at 10:00. Acknowledge refuses outright on a stale record, naming both shas, and a receiver that reads as the outgoing owner is refused at both ends.
end_to_end_flow.who: Night Dev BE prepares, Full Stack lead acknowledges or rejects with a reason
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: sbe handover show, then acknowledge --receiver <name> or reject --receiver <name> --reason "CartSync consumer not updated". The derived half is real: what is done, what is in flight, what was never started, which worktrees hold uncommitted work, which receipts are stale. The half that matters most at 06:00, the open question, is typed by a human or it is not there.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: 12-handover.json carrying an acknowledgement or a rejection with a named reason, bound to a commit. Nothing stops the lead merging or deploying while ignoring the record entirely.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 11. Pull request into main. The existing rules are untouched: minimum two reviewers with Tech Lead approval, status checks, linear history, no force push, three-level review (Technical, Security, Business). The BrotherSBE stages run advisory first and only block once the team has written them and bound a Bitbucket merge check to the build key.
end_to_end_flow.who: Jenkins agent on the PR-open and push-to-PR-branch triggers; the second BA reads the converge verdict; the Full Stack lead gives the Tech Lead approval
end_to_end_flow.system: Bitbucket and Jenkins. BrotherSBE ships no CODEOWNERS, no branch permissions, no merge checks and no Jenkinsfile. Its reference workflow is GitHub Actions, which is unusable here.
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: bin/sbe impact, tools/sbe_design.py --strict, tools/sbe_gate.py --strict, tools/sbe_score.py --strict --strict-soft, bin/sbe converge --base <kickoff sha> --head $GIT_COMMIT, bin/sbe review-route. converge compares the diff to the dossier along scope, contracts, data, architecture and verification, and has no force flag. Its source extension set contains no .cs, no .tsx and no .jsx, so on this estate the Order and Cart service changes land in a category it reports as unmeasured rather than as a verdict.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: A build status key on the source commit, verdict blocks in the build description, and two human approvals in Bitbucket. BrotherSBE cannot merge, cannot approve, and cannot tell that an approval was owed.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 12. Merge to master, then auto-deploy to Staging. Receipts and gates are commit-bound and this repo enforces linear history, so a pre-rebase receipt FAILs at the merge commit and the pipeline regenerates receipts on the post-rebase head. The QC staging suites are wrapped in the evidence runner.
end_to_end_flow.who: Jenkins CD job; QC engineer on the staging automation lane names which command counts as the check
end_to_end_flow.system: Tokyo EKS, Helm, secrets from Vault
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: SBE_CI_RUN_ID=$BUILD_TAG bin/sbe evidence run --check e2e-staging (and the performance and security equivalents), then bin/sbe evidence verify. Trust level tops out at CI-CLAIMED, which the module's own text defines as CI-shaped metadata that nothing verified: a laptop exporting the same variable on a clean tree gets the same label, and the seal is a checksum, not a signature.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: A set of receipts bound to the release commit and to declared covered paths, archived as build artifacts outside the tree they cover.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 13. Pre-Production. The migration is rehearsed forward and reverse against a restored copy at production-like volume, and the reconciliation is run on both sides of the sync boundary: a count out of Pimcore, and a differently worded count against SQL Server and against the Elasticsearch index after reindex. UAT acceptance is walked row by row against 07-verification.md, and a rejection names a failing row.
end_to_end_flow.who: PIM schema owner and a Development engineer for the rehearsal; QC pre-production lane and the Operations Consultants for acceptance
end_to_end_flow.system: Tokyo EKS dedicated node groups, restored SQL Server and Pimcore copy
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: migration-receipt.json (a receipt with no row counts is NO-DATA, and NO-DATA is never a pass) and numbers-manifest.json with a pinned snapshot_id, a second derivation whose text differs beyond case, whitespace, comments and trailing punctuation, and two numbers that match. The numbers gate executes nothing: it has no database connectivity and the figures are transcribed by a human. It proves the two derivations differ in TEXT, never that they are independent, so two counts taken downstream of the same broken ProductSync agree and are both wrong.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: Two receipt files plus a walked acceptance table. Nothing resolves the rehearsal id against Jenkins or any job system; it is a pointer for a human.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 14. Production. The Jenkins manual approval opens with a one hour timeout. Immediately before the input step a stage re-runs the gates and the team status against the release commit and writes them to the build description, so the approver reads verdicts bound to the exact commit rather than a recollection from a chat thread. The Pimcore publish of the actual field values is a separate act that never traverses Development, Staging or Pre-Production at all.
end_to_end_flow.who: Head of Project clicks Proceed. The PIM schema owner publishes in Pimcore.
end_to_end_flow.system: Jenkins CD, Helm rolling update on Tokyo EKS; Pimcore admin UI for the data half
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: bin/sbe status . --team plus a re-run of bin/sbe gate --strict, archived and written to currentBuild.description. Say this once and plainly: the Jenkins input approval and the BrotherSBE approval gate are two different approvals, and calling them one is the most dangerous sentence available here. BrotherSBE never gets apply rights, cannot deploy, cannot approve, cannot merge, never learns the click happened, and cannot see the one hour clock. It drafts the command and its rollback for a human to run.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: A deployed release, a Sentry release tag carrying the commit sha, and a build artifact holding the evidence pack. No receipt describes production state, so a CS Specialist asking whether the fix is live cannot get that answer from BrotherSBE.

end_to_end_flow.stage: 15. Back round to the next iteration. When the retailer reports the price is still wrong, the join runs backwards: Sentry release, to commit sha, to design/pim-case-price-field/, to the ADR that says why Pimcore owns the field and the flip condition that would change it. The claim that had no check gets a row added to 07-verification.md, and the tier mix and check selection get argued with against four weeks of this team's own real output.
end_to_end_flow.who: Full Stack lead and Integration Manager on the technical join; the PM and the two BAs on the retune
end_to_end_flow.sbe_artifact_or_check: sbe lineage <artifact> walks binding, receipts, decisions, notes and commits with an evidence pointer per hop. Nothing in BrotherSBE reads Sentry, Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch, ELK or Alertmanager, so the Sentry-release-name-equals-commit-sha convention is maintained by hand and computed by nothing. There is no post-deploy verification, no error budget awareness and no rollback trigger.
end_to_end_flow.handoff_out: An updated dossier and a retuned set of tier boundaries. Every threshold BrotherSBE ships was measured on ONE estate, never on a two-timezone team with a night shift, so this stage is where the defaults stop being borrowed.

seams: THE TIMEZONE SEAM, and it is the one that matters. Tokyo evening to offshore night, and 06:00 JST back to Tokyo. Today the artifact that crosses is a sentence in a chat window, which nobody can query later and which cannot settle the question of what was finished, what was half done, what was never started and what question was left open. With BrotherSBE two files cross instead: the work brief (byte-identical JSON carrying scope, mustNotTouch, dependencies, acceptance, verificationCommands, stopConditions and baselineCommit) going out, and 12-handover.json coming back, with acknowledge refusing on a stale record and refusing a self-handover. What crossing this seam still does NOT do: it notifies nobody, wakes nobody, enforces no response time, and writes openQuestions, decisions and requiredAccess EMPTY for a human to fill. Ownership moves in a JSON file two people agreed to read, not in any system. And the reason it is the most important seam is unchanged by any of this: the two BAs and the Integration Manager who can answer intent questions are asleep for the whole offshore build window, so a stop condition converts an eight hour stall into a written escalation, and nothing converts it into an answer.

THE PIMCORE ADMIN UI TO GIT SEAM. A field retyped and saved in the Pimcore admin UI in the Japan afternoon crosses no seam at all: no diff, no pull request, no Jenkins run, no SonarQube decoration, no reviewer, no gate. Every BrotherSBE check, detector and gate reads a git diff, a JSON file or a markdown file, and nothing notices the omission. The artifact that has to cross is an exported class definition committed under a path a detector matches, produced by an export job the team builds and BrotherSBE does not ship. Until that job exists, everything downstream of this seam is inert for the CONTENT group, and the honest answer is that BrotherSBE does nothing for them. Even after it exists, only the SHAPE half crosses: the Pimcore publish of the values still reaches production without traversing Development, Staging or Pre-Production.

THE CONTENT TO PRODUCT SEAM, where the system of record is decided. Product master in Pimcore, price in the Product service SQL Server tables, a derived Elasticsearch index, a Redis cache, editorial copy in Strapi that also carries product-shaped fields, read by three client apps. The artifact that crosses is 05-data-model.md, and the datamodel check FAILs any entity with no named system of record and any relationship with no cardinality. What it cannot do is tell a correct answer from a confident wrong one: writing Strapi where the truth is Pimcore passes. Cardinality is the specific trap on this business, because product variant to SKU to retailer contract price list is many-to-many and gets implemented as one-to-many by whoever writes the sync first, discovered when a retailer sees a price from someone else's contract.

THE PUBLISHER TO CONSUMER SEAM inside the change itself. The Pimcore field feeds ProductSync, which writes SQL Server, which Order Service and Cart Service read and which the Elasticsearch index is derived from. Nothing here reads a .NET DTO, an Ocelot route file, a RabbitMQ binding, a message shape, a dead letter policy or a Helm chart, and converge cannot even classify the .cs file that implements the consumer. There is no consumer impact analysis and no deploy-ordering check for a publisher and its consumer. The only artifact that crosses this seam is the handoff row a human typed into 02-process.md, which is unchecked prose. This seam is where the two blind spots overlap: the impact detectors read path names, so a queue contract change inside a C# service whose path carries no trigger word is invisible, and the silent-failure linter cannot read that file either.

THE REPOSITORY TO NON-REPOSITORY-USER SEAM. Contractor Operations Consultants, the CS Specialists and most of the commercial group have no Bitbucket account, and the dossier lives in the repository. Their own words go into 01-purpose.md and the acceptance rows go into 07-verification.md, and they cannot open either. The artifact that has to cross is a published readable copy, on merge, to somewhere without a repository account. BrotherSBE ships nothing that does this, and until somebody builds it the crossing is a BA emailing files.

THE MERGE AND REBASE SEAM. Receipts and gate verdicts are commit-bound and strict about it, and this repository enforces linear history. A receipt minted on a feature branch tip FAILs at the merge commit, and a covered file rewritten after the run (a checkout, a formatter, even with identical bytes) invalidates it. The artifact that crosses is a receipt regenerated by the pipeline on the post-rebase head, written outside the tree it covers, because a receipt written into that tree makes it dirty and demotes the next one to advisory.

THE CI TO PRODUCTION-APPROVAL SEAM. The artifact that crosses is an evidence pack: bin/sbe status . --team plus the four gate verdicts re-run against the release commit, archived and written into the build description immediately before the Jenkins input step. Two hard limits on this crossing. The Jenkins input approval and the BrotherSBE approval gate are two different approvals, and the gate verdicts in the pack are the same verdicts that already passed at PR time, so re-running them proves the commit is unchanged, not that Staging behaved. And for a T0 promotion, which is most of them, the pack is close to empty and the approver is back to reading a build number.

THE PRODUCTION TO NEXT-ITERATION SEAM. The artifact that should cross is a commit sha: Sentry release name equal to the commit that Jenkins already pushes, and design/<change>/ reachable from that sha, so an incident walks back to a commit and a commit walks back to a dossier and its ADR. Nothing computes or enforces this. BrotherSBE reads no Sentry, no Prometheus, no Grafana, no CloudWatch, no ELK and no Alertmanager, performs no post-deploy verification, and has no answer to the question this team actually asks, which is whether the fix is live in production.
jenkins_stages: ADVISORY PHASE, stage 1 of the PR job, sbe-triage. Runs on every PR open and every push to the PR branch, wrapped in catchError(buildResult: 'SUCCESS', stageResult: 'UNSTABLE'). Command: bin/sbe impact . --base origin/master (no --intake, no --strict). Purpose is to print a tier floor from path names and export it as a Jenkins variable that later stages gate on with when{}. This stage exists so a T0 change costs nothing: BrotherSBE ships no pipeline file, no when{} condition and no skip logic, so this branching is the Full Stack lead's work. Prerequisites that bite on day one: python3 at 3.9 or newer on the agent (a .NET SDK image does not have it, so change the image or route the SBE stages to a dedicated agent label), and a non-shallow clone with tags, because the approval gate later reads commit trailers and signatures.

ADVISORY PHASE, stage 2, sbe-install-verify. Command: sh scripts/verify-install.sh. Confirms the checked-out plugin matches the manifest shipped with its pinned ref, in both directions. It catches drift and accident. It is not a defence against somebody who edits the manifest too. Keep it wrapped for the first sprint like everything else.

ADVISORY PHASE, stage 3, sbe-score, the only SBE stage most pull requests on this estate will ever feel. Command: python3 tools/sbe_score.py --strict --strict-soft . run in parallel with the existing SonarQube stage and never replacing it. Verified at tools/sbe_score.py:655, SCANNABLE is (".py", ".sql", ".swift", ".rb", ".js", ".ts", ".go"). There is no .cs, so the six .NET services, the five queue processors and the four cron jobs are outside it. There is no .tsx and no .jsx either, so confirm the real extensions in the shop and portal repositories before promising the front end anything. A run that opened no file is NO-DATA naming why, never clean. Never soften this stage with || true or set +e: a discarded exit code is the exact defect class this linter exists to catch.

CONDITIONAL PHASE, stage 4, sbe-impact-strict. Runs only when stage 1 printed a floor above T0. Command: bin/sbe impact . --base origin/master --intake design/<change>/00-intake.json --strict. Catches a change touching helm/, charts/, k8s/, kubernetes/, .tf, .tfvars, docker-compose, a Jenkinsfile, a production-config path, a path containing rabbitmq, or an exported schema under schemas/, that was declared T0. It reads PATH NAMES, not code. It may raise a tier and may never lower one, and it reports consumers under unmeasured.

CONDITIONAL PHASE, stage 5, sbe-design. Runs only at T2 and T3. Command: python3 tools/sbe_design.py --strict design/<change>, then bin/sbe plan design/<change>. Fails a shipped-template file left in place, an ADR without two distinct rejected alternatives and a flip condition, an entity with no system of record, a relationship with no cardinality, a diagram node tracing to no declared entity, and an empty plan. It checks that the artifacts exist and are structurally complete, never that they are true, and a dossier written after the code passes identically. Leave SBE_DOSSIER_ROOT UNSET on these repositories: a declared root holding no dossier is a FAIL by design, which turns every routine T0 change red.

CONDITIONAL PHASE, stage 6, sbe-gate. Runs only where a dossier exists. Two commands in one stage, in this order: gpg --import of the approver public keyring fetched with the same Vault step the deploy already uses, then python3 tools/sbe_gate.py --strict design/<change>. Without the imported keys git reports %G? = E and every signed approval reads NO-DATA. A self-generated SSH signing key reports U, also NO-DATA. The keyless Reviewed-in: <Bitbucket PR id> path is NO-DATA because nothing resolves the id. On this estate the ONLY passing approval path is a host-verified signature carrying an Approved-by trailer naming somebody other than the author and committer, so self-approval fails. Public keys are not secret: Vault here is central distribution and rotation, not confidentiality. Note the exit-code fine print before relying on this stage: --strict exits nonzero on FAIL, and a NO-DATA verdict prints and exits 0, so a change that declares no migration receipt, no approval trailer and no numbers manifest produces three NO-DATA lines and a green build.

CD PHASE, stage 7, sbe-evidence on the merge-to-master job, before auto-deploy to Staging. Commands: SBE_CI_RUN_ID=$BUILD_TAG bin/sbe evidence run --check <id> --kind gate --out <a path OUTSIDE the tree the check covers> per registered QC suite, then bin/sbe evidence verify per receipt. Regenerate on the post-rebase head, because a pre-rebase receipt FAILs at the merge commit under this repository's linear history rule. Each suite needs a .sbe/checks.yml entry that QC writes and maintains, and editing that entry invalidates receipts minted before the edit. Understand the ceiling: the printed level is CI-CLAIMED, which means a run id was recorded on a clean tree and nothing verified who set it. Any laptop exporting the same variable gets the same label; the protection is that Jenkins is the only place the team sets it.

CD PHASE, stage 8, sbe-converge, immediately before auto-deploy to Staging. Command: bin/sbe converge design/<change> --base <the commit the design was implemented from> --head $GIT_COMMIT. Compares the diff to the approved dossier across scope, contracts, data, architecture and verification, and there is no force flag. Its source extension set contains no .cs, no .tsx and no .jsx, so on a .NET plus modern front end estate a large share of the diff is reported as unmeasured rather than as a verdict. It has nothing to say about a change that never carried a dossier.

CD PHASE, stage 9, sbe-promotion-pack, immediately before the existing input step with its one hour timeout. Commands: re-run python3 tools/sbe_gate.py --strict design/<change> and bin/sbe status . --team against the release commit, archiveArtifacts the output, and write the blocker-first summary into currentBuild.description so it sits on the same page as the Proceed button. BrotherSBE assembles the pack and exits. It never calls input, never approves, never deploys, never learns what was clicked, and cannot see or extend the one hour clock.

ENFORCEMENT, which is not a stage but the step that makes the stages matter. Unwrap catchError one stage at a time in the order score, impact, design and gate, converge, after two sprints of reading real verdicts against this codebase's own idioms. Then a Bitbucket admin binds a merge check of the class 'minimum successful builds on the source commit' to the SBE build status key, on top of the existing minimum two reviewers, Tech Lead approval, linear history and no force push. What that merge check CAN require: a green named build key on the exact source commit. What it CANNOT do: read the difference between FAIL and NO-DATA, require that a named evidence artifact exists, or compare an approver identity against the commit author. Check names differ between Bitbucket Cloud and Data Center, so confirm them in your own instance. Do NOT put bin/sbe work check in the blocking path: a developer who never registered gives it nothing to read. And decide the hotfix/xxx path before enforcement, not during a 03:00 JST outage, because a gate that blocks an incident fix gets waived once and then quietly deleted.
rollout: WEEK 1, no tooling, no pipeline, one number. Take the last four weeks of real requests and score each one with python3 tools/sbe_intake.py on a laptop. Publish the T0/T1/T2/T3 mix. This is the smallest possible first step and it is the one that decides whether to continue: the entire defence of this method is that T0 owes nothing and is the common case, and nobody has measured that on this team. If the mix skews to T2 and T3, the two Business Analysts become the bottleneck for the whole pipeline and the answer is to stop here or to re-argue the tier boundaries first. Also settle two access questions in the same week, before they become gaps in a later report: do the offshore QC engineers have Claude Code and a repository checkout, and where does BROTHERSBE_VAULT point on each machine and agent (it is unset by default, nothing syncs it between the two sites, and bin/sbe doctor reports NO-DATA on it by name).

WEEK 2, the timezone handover only, on one change, nothing else. The PM mints a work brief per task with sbe work brief --json and the night shift opens its shift on that instead of a scrollback. At end of shift the night dev runs sbe handover prepare and the Full Stack lead runs acknowledge or reject in the morning. No Jenkins, no gates, no dossier. This works on day one because it is only files in git read at a specific commit. Judge it on one question at the end of the week: did an ambiguity that would have cost a 24 hour round trip get recorded as a stop condition and an open question instead. Remember openQuestions is written empty, so the night dev has to type it.

WEEK 3, one dossier on one real change above T0. Pick the PIM price field change, not a toy. The BA writes purpose, process and verification; the Integration Manager writes the data model and one ADR; the second BA runs python3 tools/sbe_design.py --strict and refutes it. Everything by hand on laptops. Expect the data model to be the artifact that produces the argument, and expect that argument to be the actual value delivered this week.

WEEK 4 to 5, build the Pimcore export job. This is engineering work with no BrotherSBE in it and it is the prerequisite for the CONTENT group existing in this flow at all. Export the class definition to schemas/pimcore/Product.json, mirror the Strapi content-type to schemas/strapi/<type>.json (its own file is named schema.json under content-types/<type>/, which the shipped detector does not match because it requires a DIRECTORY named event, events, schema or schemas), commit on a branch, open a PR. Confirm the export command and the on-disk path against the installed Pimcore version rather than assuming. In the same window, nominate the PIM schema owner. If the CONTENT group will not staff that role, stop and say plainly that BrotherSBE does nothing for CONTENT.

WEEK 6, the first Jenkins stage, and only one: sbe-score, wrapped in catchError(buildResult: 'SUCCESS', stageResult: 'UNSTABLE'). Sort out python3 on the agent or a dedicated agent label, and switch the checkout to full history with tags. Measure the added wall clock on every push, because the PR pipeline already runs build, tests, Gitleaks, SonarQube, Trivy and packaging, and a slow merge path gets bypassed. Read the false positives against this codebase's own idioms.

WEEK 7, add sbe-triage (bin/sbe impact with no --strict) and the when{} logic that keeps T0 changes free of everything else, still advisory. The test of this week is negative: if a T0 change ever goes red for a missing artifact, the pipeline is wired wrong and gets fixed before anything else proceeds.

WEEK 8, the keyring. A Development engineer puts the approvers' public keys in Vault and imports them in a gate stage, and one reviewer signs one commit with an Approved-by trailer to prove git reports %G? = G on the agent. Until this exists the approval gate is permanently NO-DATA on this estate, so this is the week that decides whether the approval gate is ever real here. Decide separately, and write it down as a decision, whether a commercial product owner who never touches git will ever hold a signing key, because if not the Pre-Production UAT sign-off stays a human record indefinitely.

WEEK 9, wrap ONE QC suite in the evidence runner on the Staging job, with SBE_CI_RUN_ID=$BUILD_TAG and the receipt written outside the tree it covers, plus its .sbe/checks.yml entry owned by a named QC engineer. Add bin/sbe evidence verify. Confirm in the same week that a pre-rebase receipt FAILs at the merge commit, so the regeneration step is designed rather than discovered.

WEEK 10, build the migration rehearsal job against a restored copy in Pre-Production: forward, reverse, row counts on both sides, a rehearsal id, emitting migration-receipt.json. This is the job that would have caught a broken rollback hours before the one hour production window instead of inside it. BrotherSBE reads the receipt and produces none of it, and nothing resolves the rehearsal id against Jenkins.

WEEK 11, unwrap sbe-score to blocking and have a Bitbucket admin bind the merge check to the SBE build status key. This is the first week anything actually stops a merge, and Bitbucket does the stopping, not BrotherSBE. Decide and document the hotfix/xxx path in the same change, before an incident forces the decision.

WEEK 12, unwrap impact, then design and gate, one at a time, only on the T2 and T3 path. Add sbe-converge before the Staging deploy, and the promotion pack before the input step. Then stop adding and retune: re-score the tier mix against the real twelve weeks, argue the tier boundaries, and record what you changed and why. Every threshold shipped was measured on ONE estate, and adopting here makes this team the second data point.
what_this_does_not_fix: It does not shrink the timezone. sbe handover records that a named human acknowledged ownership at a specific commit and refuses a stale or self-handover. It notifies nobody, wakes nobody, enforces no response time, and reject leaves the work with the outgoing owner. The two BAs and the Integration Manager are still asleep during the whole offshore build window, so an ambiguity that needs their judgment is still an eight hour wait. What changes is that it becomes a written escalation instead of an undocumented guess.

It blocks nothing on its own. Every gate is a command that prints a verdict and, with --strict, exits nonzero. Three separate pieces of the team's own wiring sit between a FAIL and a stopped merge: a Jenkins stage they write, a Bitbucket merge check an admin binds, and the branch permissions they already have. BrotherSBE ships no CODEOWNERS, no branch protection, no merge checks and no CI configuration, and its reference workflow is GitHub Actions, which is unusable here. Until those stages exist, adopting it changes what people write, not what CI does.

It cannot see absent evidence, only declared evidence. The migration gate returns NO-DATA with the literal reason "no migration in this change, or no migration-receipt.json" and cannot tell those two apart. Nothing detects that a change NEEDED an approval, a receipt or a dossier. Worse for anyone reading a clean run as safety: --strict exits nonzero only on FAIL, so a change that declares nothing at all produces NO-DATA lines and a green build. NO-DATA is never a pass as a verdict and is not a block as an exit code.

It does not read C#, which is most of this estate. The silent-failure linter's scannable set is pinned at tools/sbe_score.py:655 to .py .sql .swift .rb .js .ts .go. No .cs, so Identity, Product, Customer, Order, User, Cart, the five queue processors and the four cron jobs are invisible to it. No .tsx and no .jsx either, so if the shop and portal apps are React it reads almost none of the front end. converge and the impact detectors cannot classify a .cs file either, so a .NET change lands in an explicitly unmeasured category rather than a verdict. SonarQube stays the only automated reader of the backend, and no configuration closes this.

It proves nothing about whether two derivations are independent. The numbers gate proves two texts differ beyond case, whitespace, comments and trailing punctuation, and that two transcribed figures match. It executes no query, has no database connectivity and cannot tell a transcribed number from an invented one. Two counts taken downstream of the same broken ProductSync agree and are both wrong, and two reads of the same stale Elasticsearch index pass. On pricing, rebate and reconciliation work that is a live exposure, not a theoretical one.

It cannot see Pimcore, Strapi, Klaviyo, Voucherify, Branch.io or LINE Connect. Everything reads a git diff, a JSON file or a markdown file. A field saved in the Pimcore admin UI, a campaign built in Klaviyo, a voucher rule, a deep link, a content-type published from Strapi: none of them pass through a diff, so none gets a design phase, a gate, a linter or a receipt, and nothing notices the omission. A large share of what Sales and CS log as bugs is product data or content, not code. Say this on day one, not after a miss.

The data model check verifies that a system of record is NAMED and a cardinality is STATED, never that either is correct. Writing Strapi where the truth is Pimcore passes every check that ships. The same holds for the ADR: the shape is checked (two distinct rejected alternatives, a flip condition present), the judgment is not. Nothing reads 01-purpose.md, 02-process.md, 04-technology-map.md or 07-verification.md for content at all, so a thin dossier written to clear the gate clears the gate, and converge then compares the diff against that thin thing.

The tier is computed from five answers a human typed. The rule is fixed and unarguable; the inputs are checked against nothing at intake time. A BA or a Marketing lead who answers no to the money or personal-data question gets T0 and owes nothing. sbe impact can raise a tier later, never lower one, but it reasons from path names after code exists: its money detector matches pricing, discount and invoice, not the bare word price, so PriceList.json raises to T2 and no further, and a Klaviyo sync written inside existing service code may trip nothing at all.

There is no write fence for humans. The scope comparison lives in a Claude Code PreToolUse hook whose own rule is fail open, loudly, so it binds nobody typing in Rider, Visual Studio or VS Code, and nothing binds git apply or a shell redirect. sbe work start refuses a taken branch, a taken worktree path and a re-opened task id, and never compares file scopes between two different tasks. Two Japan front end developers and the Night Dev FE holding the same cart components get a registry a human reads, not a refusal.

It never gets apply rights on production. It cannot deploy, cannot approve, cannot merge, cannot publish or unpublish a Pimcore object, cannot trigger a re-sync or a reindex. It drafts the command and its rollback for a human to run. The Jenkins input approval and its one hour timeout are exactly as human as before, and BrotherSBE never learns the click happened. No receipt describes production state, so the question CS actually asks, is it live and is it fixed, has no answer here today or after wiring.

It reads no telemetry and does nothing after the rolling update starts. No Sentry, Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch, ELK or Alertmanager. No post-deploy verification, no error budget awareness, no rollback trigger. It does not test the Osaka failover, the sub four hour target, the DNS redirect or the daily encrypted backups, and the restored copy in a migration receipt is one the team made, not the DR replica.

It replaces no human review, no standup, no decision and no person. The two-reviewer plus Tech Lead rule stays entirely Bitbucket's. review-route prints at most two suggested specialist roles from the diff, adds nobody to a pull request, and does not know who is awake. sbe status --team shows only changes somebody recorded and is blind to the rest, so it is a view of the process, not of the work. The specialist reviewers and the evidence auditor produce model-written prose that persuades a human and computes nothing.

The spine, design before verification and install the check before writing the work, is a stated discipline that no tool computes and that Jenkins cannot enforce across days. A complete dossier written after the code passes every gate identically. If the team stops writing dossiers, every verdict degrades to NO-DATA, which does not block, and the whole apparatus becomes files nobody maintains.

The cost is real and lands on named people who are already the bottleneck. A T3 change owes seven hand-written artifacts from two BAs. The Jenkinsfile, the Helm charts and the Bitbucket configuration are a second hat worn by the Full Stack lead and the Integration Manager, both in Japan, maintaining a pipeline that runs code written offshore overnight. The CONTENT group needs a PIM schema owner who does not exist today, and a four-minute Pimcore rename becomes an export, a branch, an intake, a dossier and a wait for a second human. The first month costs time before it saves any.

Every threshold shipped was measured on ONE estate, never this one, never a .NET microservice estate, never a Pimcore or Strapi installation, and never a two-timezone team with a night shift. The handover, evidence, impact and converge surfaces are marked INTERNAL-EVAL in the project's own documentation: they ran against its own fixtures and its own diff. Adopting here makes this team the second data point, which is exactly why the advisory phase is not optional.
